ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p238/r6.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p238/r6.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p238/r6.claim: The sūrah's final divine attributes encourage submission and trust in strong believers, resolve and confidence in weak believers, and fear of God in hypocrites; the ending returns to the opening note.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p238/r6.anchor: The sūrah finally ends on the note it began

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p258/r5.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p258/r5.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p258/r5.claim: Although the closing passage addresses Muslims generally, its context directs it especially to the hypocrites discussed from the sūrah's beginning.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p258/r5.anchor: Though, by the words used, they address common Muslims

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p259/r2.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p259/r2.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p259/r2.claim: People should reflect on God's attributes and bring their inner and outward lives, beliefs, deeds, and hoped-for outcome into harmony with them.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p259/r2.anchor: they should assess and evaluate their present and future, their good and evil, their beliefs and deeds

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p263/r3.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p263/r3.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p263/r3.claim: After mentioning fear of God, the passage names His attributes so believers, disbelievers, and hypocrites can understand how to fear, love, hope in, trust, and serve Him.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p263/r3.anchor: so that the believers, the disbelievers and the hypocrites, all come to know of these attributes.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p263/r4.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p263/r4.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p263/r4.claim: The attributes of God and their implications form the basis of religion and sharīʿah; Qur'anic commands are manifestations of them, so full understanding requires the whole Qur'an.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p263/r4.anchor: the basis of the sharī‘ah and religion is the attributes of God and what these attributes entail.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p267/r1.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p267/r1.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p267/r1.claim: Creation unfolds in a first phase of design and planning, termed khalq.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p267/r1.anchor: The first phase is that of design and plan. The Arabic word used for it is ﺧﻠﻖ

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p267/r2.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p267/r2.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p267/r2.claim: The second phase brings a planned thing into existence, termed barʾ.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p267/r2.anchor: The second phase is to bring it into existence. The Arabic word used for it is ﺑﺮء

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p267/r3.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p267/r3.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p267/r3.claim: The third phase perfects and models the thing, termed taṣwīr.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p267/r3.anchor: The third phase is to perfect it. The Arabic word used for it is ﺗﺼﻮﻳﺮ.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p267/r4.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p267/r4.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p267/r4.claim: Since God alone carries out all phases of creation without help, He alone deserves glorification and worship.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p267/r4.anchor: He alone is worthy of being glorified and worshipped by all.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p267/r5.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p267/r5.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p267/r5.claim: The names mentioned are basic divine attributes, and every other beautiful name of God also expresses an attribute He possesses.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p267/r5.anchor: All names of God express one or the other attribute He possesses.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p267/r6.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p267/r6.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p267/r6.claim: Because God creates all things, everything in heaven and earth glorifies Him; a person who refuses by choice rejects truth arrogantly and should worship God alone.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p267/r6.anchor: this is an act of not acknowledging the truth, and arrogance on his part.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p267/r7.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p267/r7.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p267/r7.claim: The ending recalls God's opening attributes: He has power to compel worship, but in wisdom grants humans free will to test whether they recognize His right or serve Satan.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p267/r7.anchor: He wanted to test whether, after being granted with this status, he recognises the right of God on him

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p149/r1.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p149/r1.speaker: علي وحاطب بن أبي بلتعة والحسن وابن السميقع
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p149/r1.claim: ʿAlī, Ḥāṭib, al-Ḥasan, and Ibn al-Sumayqiʿ read المصور with fatḥa on wāw and rāʾ, as an object of al-Bāriʾ referring to things fashioned.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p149/r1.anchor: وقرأ علي وحاطب بن أبي بلتعة والحسن وابن السميقع: المصور بفتح الواو والراء

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p149/r2.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p149/r2.speaker: علي
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p149/r2.claim: ʿAlī also reads wāw with fatḥa and rāʾ with kasra, making the active participle annexed to its object.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p149/r2.anchor: وعن علي فتح الواو وكسر الراء على إضافة اسم الفاعل إلى المفعول

STUDYQURAN:57:intro/r3.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:57:intro/r3.speaker: the Prophet
STUDYQURAN:57:intro/r3.claim: A hadith says one verse among the Glorifiers is better than a thousand verses; some identify it as 57:3, others as the last verse of al-Hashr.
STUDYQURAN:57:intro/r3.anchor: Within [the Glorifiers] there is a verse that is better than a thousand verses

ELMALILI:59:22-24#3/r11.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:59:22-24#3/r11.speaker: author
ELMALILI:59:22-24#3/r11.claim: God alone is the Creator, while everything else is created; khalq can mean determining things’ measures and ranks or bringing the nonexistent into being, and sometimes making one thing from another.
ELMALILI:59:22-24#3/r11.anchor: Yukarılarda birkaç kereler geçtiği vechile bizim “yaratmak” tâbir ettiğimiz halk fiili iki mâna ifade eder. Birisi takdir etmek, yani eşyânın bütün tafsîlâtıyla mikdar ve merâtibini tâyin [4876] eylemektir.

ELMALILI:59:22-24#3/r12.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:59:22-24#3/r12.speaker: author
ELMALILI:59:22-24#3/r12.claim: Complete determination requires knowledge of every thing’s measure and rank among all things; this is why khalq is usually used of things with measure and quantity.
ELMALILI:59:22-24#3/r12.anchor: Zira bir şeyi tamamıyla takdir etmek onun bütün eşyâ arasındaki mikdar ve mertebesini bilmeye, bu da hepsini tamamıyla bilmeye mütevakkıftır.

ELMALILI:59:22-24#3/r13.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:59:22-24#3/r13.speaker: author
ELMALILI:59:22-24#3/r13.claim: The highest human arts remain bounded discovery and construction under God’s determination: people cannot fully determine a created act or bring even an atom into existence, so only God truly creates.
ELMALILI:59:22-24#3/r13.anchor: Mahluklara nisbet edilebilen en yüksek sanatlar, Allah teâlâ’nın takdir buyurduğu keşf ü inşâ mâhiyetinden ileri geçemez.

ELMALILI:59:22-24#3/r14.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:59:22-24#3/r14.speaker: author
ELMALILI:59:22-24#3/r14.claim: Al-Bari is the clean Creator who selects, orders, shapes, and perfects what He creates, distinguishing creatures by different qualities and properties.
ELMALILI:59:22-24#3/r14.anchor: Bâri’ yani öyle temiz yaratıcı ki halkettiklerini temiz ve sağlam bir nizam üzere seçip tesviye ve tekâmül ettirerek birbirinden farklı evsâf ve havâs ile temeyyüz[^40] ettirir.

ELMALILI:59:22-24#3/r15.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:59:22-24#3/r15.speaker: Mefâtîhü’l-Gayb
ELMALILI:59:22-24#3/r15.claim: Mafatih al-Ghayb distinguishes al-Bari from maker and originator by saying it denotes originating corporeal bodies, not accidents such as color or taste.
ELMALILI:59:22-24#3/r15.anchor: Mefâtîhü’l-Gayb’da der ki: “‘Bâri’’ ismi, ‘sâni‘’ ve ‘mûcid’ gibi olmakla beraber ecsâmın ihtirâ‘ını ifade eder.

ELMALILI:59:22-24#3/r16.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:59:22-24#3/r16.speaker: author
ELMALILI:59:22-24#3/r16.claim: The supplication joining the verbs create, disperse, and bring forth suggests that al-Bari concerns acts of bringing creation to completion.
ELMALILI:59:22-24#3/r16.anchor: bazı ed‘iye-i me’sûrede[^42] vârid olan “halaka” ve “zere’e” ve “bere’e” fiillerine nazaran “Bâri’” ism-i şerîfi hilkatin tekâmül mertebelerindeki îcadlara nâzır olduğu anlaşılıyor.

ELMALILI:59:22-24#3/r17.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:59:22-24#3/r17.speaker: author
ELMALILI:59:22-24#3/r17.claim: Al-Musawwir alone determines and creates the forms and qualities of creatures as He wills.
ELMALILI:59:22-24#3/r17.anchor: Musavvir, O mahlûkātın suret ve keyfiyetlerini dahi takdir edip dilediği vechile îcad ederek tasvir edici ancak O’dur.

ELMALILI:59:22-24#3/r18.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:59:22-24#3/r18.speaker: Râgıb
ELMALILI:59:22-24#3/r18.claim: Raghib defines form as what imprints an entity and distinguishes it from others, and divides forms into sensory and intelligible kinds.
ELMALILI:59:22-24#3/r18.anchor: Râgıb der ki: [4877] “‘Sûret’, a‘yânın kendisiyle müntekış olup sâirlerinden temeyyüz ettiği ne ise odur. Bu da iki türlüdür.

ELMALILI:59:22-24#3/r19.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:59:22-24#3/r19.speaker: author
ELMALILI:59:22-24#3/r19.claim: Sensory forms are perceived by ordinary and learned people and many animals, while intelligible forms such as reason and relational properties are perceived only by the elite; 7:11 indicates both.
ELMALILI:59:22-24#3/r19.anchor: Meselâ insana muhtas olan akıl ve reviyyet ve eşyânın birbirlerine nazaran hâssalarını ifade eden me‘ânî gibi ki وَلَقَدْ خَلَقْنَٰكُمْ ثُمَّ صَوَّرْنَٰكُمْ [el-A‘râf 7/11] gibi âyetlerde bu[^45] iki suretin ikisine de işaret olunmuştur.

ELMALILI:59:22-24#4/r1.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:59:22-24#4/r1.speaker: author
ELMALILI:59:22-24#4/r1.claim: God’s beautiful names are not limited to the ones just mentioned; all names conveying the most beautiful and exalted meanings belong to Him, as stated at 7:180 and 20:8.
ELMALILI:59:22-24#4/r1.anchor: esmâ-i hüsnâ hep O’nun, yani Allah teâlâ’nın evsâfını ifade eden isimleri bu zikrolunanlardan ibaret değildir. En güzel, en yüksek mânalara delâlet eden en güzel isimler hep O’nundur.

ELMALILI:59:22-24#4/r2.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:59:22-24#4/r2.speaker: author
ELMALILI:59:22-24#4/r2.claim: In religious usage, al-asma al-husna specifically denotes God’s names; some are names of the essence and others names of attributes.
ELMALILI:59:22-24#4/r2.anchor: “En güzel isimler” demek olan işbu “esmâ-i hüsnâ” tâbiri lisân-ı şer‘de bilhassa Allah teâlâ’nın isimlerine ıtlak olunur.

ELMALILI:59:22-24#4/r3.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:59:22-24#4/r3.speaker: author
ELMALILI:59:22-24#4/r3.claim: Allah is the sole encompassing name of the divine essence; the other names are attribute names, and al-Rahman is a special name that may not be applied to anyone else.
ELMALILI:59:22-24#4/r3.anchor: Yalnız[^47]“Allah” ism-i celâli hepsini câmi‘olan zat ismi, diğerleri sıfât ismidir. Rahmân ismi ism-i sıfat olmakla beraber Allah’tan başkasına ıtlâkı câiz olmayan hâs isimlerdendir[^48].

ELMALILI:59:22-24#4/r4.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:59:22-24#4/r4.speaker: author
ELMALILI:59:22-24#4/r4.claim: Essential attributes include negative attributes that deny likeness and affirm transcendence, such as necessary existence, pre-eternity, permanence, and dissimilarity from originated things; names such as al-Quddus and al-Salam express this.
ELMALILI:59:22-24#4/r4.anchor: Sıfât-ı selbiye vücûb-i vücûd, kıdem, bekā, muhalefetün li’l-havâdis, yani hâdisâta benzememek gibi nefy-i teşbih ile kudsiyet ve nezâhet ifade eden sıfatlardır

ELMALILI:59:22-24#4/r5.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:59:22-24#4/r5.speaker: author
ELMALILI:59:22-24#4/r5.claim: Essential affirmative attributes are life, knowledge, hearing, sight, will, power, speech, and creation, expressed in names such as Hayy, Alim, Sami, Basir, and Khaliq.
ELMALILI:59:22-24#4/r5.anchor: Sıfât-ı sübûtiye hayat, ilim, sem‘, basar, irade, kudret, kelâm, tekvin sıfatlarıdır.

ELMALILI:59:22-24#4/r6.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:59:22-24#4/r6.speaker: author
ELMALILI:59:22-24#4/r6.claim: Active attributes are manifestations of the creative attribute through its effects and rulings; examples include Creator, Originator, Fashioner, Giver of life, and Provider.
ELMALILI:59:22-24#4/r6.anchor: Sıfât-ı fi‘liye, sıfât-ı zâtiyenin âsâr ve ahkâm ile zuhûrunu ifade eden tekvin sıfatının tecelliyâtıdır ki

ELMALILI:59:22-24#4/r7.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:59:22-24#4/r7.speaker: author
ELMALILI:59:22-24#4/r7.claim: Divine names for particular acts require decorum, attention to paired opposites, and fidelity to scriptural usage rather than isolated or questionable qualifications.
ELMALILI:59:22-24#4/r7.anchor: Her fiilin husûsiyetine göre müstakillen isim ıtlâkı veya şâibeli bir kayd ile takyîdi câiz olmaz; mütekābilen nazar-ı dikkate alınmak, edeb ile cihet-i hüsn ve kemâl gözetilmek

ELMALILI:59:22-24#4/r8.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:59:22-24#4/r8.speaker: Beyhakī
ELMALILI:59:22-24#4/r8.claim: Bayhaqi cautions that al-Darr should not be mentioned alone but should be paired with al-Nafi; the Qur’an also pairs harm and benefit at 22:13.
ELMALILI:59:22-24#4/r8.anchor: Beyhakī’nin tenbih ettiği vechile “Dârr” ismi yalnız olarak söylenmez, “Nâfi‘” ismi ile beraber söylenmek lâzım gelir.

ELMALILI:59:22-24#4/r9.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:59:22-24#4/r9.speaker: author
ELMALILI:59:22-24#4/r9.claim: Al-Qabid and al-Basit are likewise paired; Qur’anic usage also joins might with retribution and al-Aziz, al-Jabbar, and al-Mutakabbir.
ELMALILI:59:22-24#4/r9.anchor: “Kâbız” ve “Bâsıt” isimleri de böyledir. Nitekim Kur’an’da يَقْبِضُ وَيَبْصُۜطُ [el-Bakara 2/245], عَزِيزٌۭ ذُو ٱنتِقَامٍۢ

ELMALILI:59:22-24#4/r10.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:59:22-24#4/r10.speaker: author
ELMALILI:59:22-24#4/r10.claim: Although God created every thing and all animals, it is irreverent to call Him simply the creator of apes and pigs.
ELMALILI:59:22-24#4/r10.anchor: Fakat sadece خَالِقُ الْقِرَدَة وَالْخَنَازِير demek câiz olmaz, edebe münâfî olur.

ELMALILI:59:22-24#4/r11.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:59:22-24#4/r11.speaker: Mu‘tezile
ELMALILI:59:22-24#4/r11.claim: The Mu‘tazila went so far as to deny that God creates evil, but the author rejects this; one should speak of Him as creator of good and evil together.
ELMALILI:59:22-24#4/r11.anchor: Bundan dolayı Mu‘tezile “Allah şerrin hâlıkı değildir” demeye kadar gitmişlerse de bu da doğru değildir.

ELMALILI:59:22-24#4/r12.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:59:22-24#4/r12.speaker: author
ELMALILI:59:22-24#4/r12.claim: Meaning attributes describe divine majesty and beauty, might, justice, wisdom, forbearance, patience, bounty, severe punishment, and swift reckoning.
ELMALILI:59:22-24#4/r12.anchor: Sıfât-ı ma‘neviye: Allah teâlâ’nın ahlâkını ve sıfât ve esmâsının ahkâm ve kemâlini ifade eden azamet ve kibriyâ, celâl ve cemâl, izzet, adalet, hikmet, hilim, sabır, fazl

ELMALILI:59:22-24#4/r13.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:59:22-24#4/r13.speaker: author
ELMALILI:59:22-24#4/r13.claim: God’s essence is one but His beautiful names are many, and the Qur’anic names mentioned here are not exhaustive.
ELMALILI:59:22-24#4/r13.anchor: Hâsılı Allah teâlâ’nın zâtı bir, esmâ-i hüsnâsı çoktur. Kur’an’da zikrolunanlar buradakilerden ibaret değildir.

ELMALILI:59:22-24#4/r14.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:59:22-24#4/r14.speaker: Ebû Hüreyre
ELMALILI:59:22-24#4/r14.claim: A sound hadith transmitted by Bukhari, Muslim, and others says that whoever enumerates God’s ninety-nine names will enter Paradise, and says God is One and loves odd numbers.
ELMALILI:59:22-24#4/r14.anchor: Buhârî, Müslim ve sâirede Ebû Hüreyre radıyallâhu anh’tan rivayet olunan bir hadîs-i sahîhte Allah teâlâ’nın doksan dokuz ismini ihsâ edenin cennete gireceği

ELMALILI:59:22-24#4/r15.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:59:22-24#4/r15.speaker: Beyhakī
ELMALILI:59:22-24#4/r15.claim: Bayhaqi gives a detailed ninety-nine-name narration from Abu Hurayra through several routes; al-Tirmidhi, Ibn Hibban, and al-Hakim also transmit it according to al-Jami al-Saghir.
ELMALILI:59:22-24#4/r15.anchor: Beyhakī[^55] Kitâbü’l-esmâi ve’s-sıfât’ta birkaç tarîk ile Ebû Hüreyre radıyallâhu anh’tan şu tafsîli rivayet etmiştir

ELMALILI:59:22-24#4/r16.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:59:22-24#4/r16.speaker: author
ELMALILI:59:22-24#4/r16.claim: God’s names established explicitly or implicitly in scripture and Sunna are not confined to the ninety-nine-name lists.
ELMALILI:59:22-24#4/r16.anchor: Ma‘amâfîh Allah teâlâ’nın[^58] Kitab ve sünnette sarâhaten veya delâleten[^59] sâbit olan isimleri bunlara da münhasır değildir.

ELMALILI:59:22-24#4/r17.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:59:22-24#4/r17.speaker: author
ELMALILI:59:22-24#4/r17.claim: Another transmitted list of ninety-nine includes further names such as al-Ilah, al-Rabb, al-Ahad, al-Jamil, al-Qarib, and al-Fatir.
ELMALILI:59:22-24#4/r17.anchor: Nitekim diğer bir rivayette sayılan doksan dokuzda şu isimler de mezkurdur: اَلاِْلٰهُ، ال َّر ُّب، الْحَن َّانُ، الْمَن َّانُ

ELMALILI:59:22-24#4/r18.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:59:22-24#4/r18.speaker: author
ELMALILI:59:22-24#4/r18.claim: The Qur’an also gives many other names and descriptions, including Lord of the worlds, Knower of unseen and seen, Forgiver of sin, Acceptor of repentance, and Doer of whatever He wills; some are exclusive to God.
ELMALILI:59:22-24#4/r18.anchor: Kur’an’da Rabbü’l-âlemîn, Rabbü’l-Arşi’l-azîm, Mâliki yevmi’d-dîn, Âlimü’l-gaybi ve’ş-şehâde, Allâmu’l-guyûb, Gāfiru’z-zenb

ELMALILI:59:22-24#4/r19.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:59:22-24#4/r19.speaker: author
ELMALILI:59:22-24#4/r19.claim: The Prophet’s invocations also use exclusive names for God, including Sender of the Book, Mover of the clouds, and Defeater of the confederates.
ELMALILI:59:22-24#4/r19.anchor: Peygamber’in Buhârî ve [4880] Müslim’de rivayet olunan dualarında Münzilü’l-Kitâb, Mücri’s-sehâb, Hâzimü’l-ahzâb[^64] isimleri de başkasına ıtlak olunamayacak isimlerdendir.

ELMALILI:59:22-24#5/r1.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:59:22-24#5/r1.speaker: İbn Kesîr
ELMALILI:59:22-24#5/r1.claim: Ibn Kathir says a hadith from Ibn Masud in Imam Ahmad’s Musnad indicates that God’s beautiful names are not limited to ninety-nine.
ELMALILI:59:22-24#5/r1.anchor: İbn Kesîr tefsirinde demiştir ki: “Esmâ-i hüsnânın doksan dokuza münhasır olmadığına İmam Ahmed b. Hanbel Hazretleri’nin Müsnedinde senediyle Abdullah b. Mes‘ûd

ELMALILI:59:22-24#5/r2.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:59:22-24#5/r2.speaker: Abdullah b. Mes‘ûd
ELMALILI:59:22-24#5/r2.claim: The Prophet taught a prayer for a Muslim in distress, asking by every divine name—including names revealed, taught, self-named, or reserved in the unseen—that the Qur’an become the heart’s spring and remove grief; God then replaces worry with joy.
ELMALILI:59:22-24#5/r2.anchor: Beyhakī de Kitâbü’l-esmâi ve’s-sıfât’ta bu hadîsi Abdullah b. Mes‘ûd Hazretleri’ne muttasıl senediyle şöyle rivayet eylemiştir

ELMALILI:59:22-24#5/r3.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:59:22-24#5/r3.speaker: Hazret-i Âişe
ELMALILI:59:22-24#5/r3.claim: Aisha asks the Prophet to teach her the name by which God answers prayer; after instructing her to perform ablution, enter the mosque, pray two cycles, and supplicate, he affirms her prayer invoking all known and unknown names and the supreme name.
ELMALILI:59:22-24#5/r3.anchor: Yine Beyhakī sened-i muttasıl ile Hazret-i Âişe radıyallâhu anhâ’dan rivayet etmiştir; Müşârün ileyhâ: “Yâ Resûlallah! Allah teâlâ’nın kendisine dua edildiği zaman icâbet

ELMALILI:59:22-24#5/r4.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:59:22-24#5/r4.speaker: author
ELMALILI:59:22-24#5/r4.claim: These prayers indicate that God has beautiful names He did not reveal in scripture or teach anyone, keeping them solely in His knowledge of the unseen.
ELMALILI:59:22-24#5/r4.anchor: Allah teâlâ’nın esmâ-i hüsnâsından Kitab’da indirmediği, kimseye bildirmediği, ilm-i gaybda yalnız kendisinin bildiği isimleri de vardır.

ELMALILI:59:22-24#5/r5.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:59:22-24#5/r5.speaker: author
ELMALILI:59:22-24#5/r5.claim: Thus the ninety-nine-name hadith means that whoever enumerates the ninety-nine knowable names—by learning and counting them or carefully observing their bounds in dealings with God—enters Paradise.
ELMALILI:59:22-24#5/r5.anchor: Allah’ın mâlum olabilen esmâ-i hüsnâsından doksan dokuzunu ihsâ eden, yani belleyip sayan yahut Allah ile muamelesinde onların hudûdunu muhafaza edip güzelce riayet eyleyen kimse cennete girer mânasına olmak gerektir.

ELMALILI:59:22-24#5/r6.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:59:22-24#5/r6.speaker: author
ELMALILI:59:22-24#5/r6.claim: The count is odd because God is One and loves odd numbers; the after-prayer remembrances of thirty-three each for glorification, praise, and magnification likewise total ninety-nine.
ELMALILI:59:22-24#5/r6.anchor: Tam yüz sayılmayıp da biri müstesnâ olarak doksan dokuz addedilmesinin hikmeti de اِن َّهُ وِتـْرٌ يُحِ ُّب الْوِتـْرَ diye beyan buyurulmuştur

ELMALILI:59:22-24#5/r7.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:59:22-24#5/r7.speaker: author
ELMALILI:59:22-24#5/r7.claim: The same hadith signals al-Witr as one of God’s names, thereby indicating a hundred names even as its enumeration omits one and further showing that the names are not limited to ninety-nine.
ELMALILI:59:22-24#5/r7.anchor: Şu da şâyân-ı dikkattir ki aynı hadiste وِتـْرٌ يُحِ ُّب الْوِتـْرَ buyurulmakla esmâullahtan birinin de اَلْوِتـْرُ olduğu iş‘âr olunarak yüz isim anlatılmış

ELMALILI:59:22-24#5/r8.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:59:22-24#5/r8.speaker: author
ELMALILI:59:22-24#5/r8.claim: Enumerating ninety-nine names has great merit for knowing God and having prayers answered, as many reports attest and dedicated works discuss, though many other names remain.
ELMALILI:59:22-24#5/r8.anchor: doksan dokuz esmâyı belleyip ihsâ etmenin marifetullah hususunda ve duanın müstecâb olmasında büyük fazileti bulunduğu vârid olan müte‘addid rivayetlerle haber verilmiş

ELMALILI:59:22-24#5/r9.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:59:22-24#5/r9.speaker: author
ELMALILI:59:22-24#5/r9.claim: Everything in the heavens and earth glorifies God, as also stated at 17:44.
ELMALILI:59:22-24#5/r9.anchor: O’na bütün göklerde ve yerde ne varsa hepsi tesbih eder, tenzih eder[^72]; وَإِن مِّن شَىْءٍ إِلَّا يُسَبِّحُ بِحَمْدِهِۦ [el-İsrâ 17/44] bak.

ELMALILI:59:22-24#5/r10.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:59:22-24#5/r10.speaker: author
ELMALILI:59:22-24#5/r10.claim: Al-Aziz and al-Hakim encompass every perfection: might is perfect power without stain, while wisdom expresses perfect knowledge and ordered creation; their manifestations appear throughout the cosmos and unite fully only in God.
ELMALILI:59:22-24#5/r10.anchor: Kemâl-i izzet hiçbir şâibe kabul etmeyen kemâl-i kudreti, kemâl-i hikmet de kemâl-i ilm ile nizâm-ı sun‘u ifade eder.

ELMALILI:59:22-24#5/r11.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:59:22-24#5/r11.speaker: author
ELMALILI:59:22-24#5/r11.claim: God’s unassailable might makes Him sovereign over all causes and able to originate incomparable wonders, while His perfect wisdom orders, diversifies, and connects creation to benefit servants through mercy.
ELMALILI:59:22-24#5/r11.anchor: Bununla beraber hiçbir noksan kabul etmeyen kemâl-i ilm ve hikmeti ile ibdâ‘âtını yekdiğerine rabtederek muntazam yollarla tenvî‘ve teksir ve bu sayede kullarını dahi hikmetten hikmete feyz-i rahmetiyle bekâm eden bir Hakîm’dir.

ELMALILI:59:22-24#5/r12.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:59:22-24#5/r12.speaker: author
ELMALILI:59:22-24#5/r12.claim: Al-Aziz al-Hakim mirrors al-Rahman al-Rahim before the declaration of transcendence; their repetition at the surah’s beginning and end links its conclusion back to its opening.
ELMALILI:59:22-24#5/r12.anchor: ٱلْعَزِيزُ ٱلْحَكِيمُ isimleri سُبْحَٰنَ ٱللَّهِ عَمَّا يُشْرِكُونَ fâsılasından evvelki ٱلرَّحْمَٰنُ ٱلرَّحِيمُ isimleriyle mütenâzır olarak âhiri evvele ircâ‘etmek üzere sûrenin evvel ve âhirinde tekrar olunmuştur.

ELMALILI:59:22-24#5/r13.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:59:22-24#5/r13.speaker: author
ELMALILI:59:22-24#5/r13.claim: People should fear offending God’s might, work toward the hereafter through faith and piety, and seek the salvation promised through His mercy by sanctifying and glorifying Him.
ELMALILI:59:22-24#5/r13.anchor: O’nun izzetine dokunmaktan korkmalı; takdis, [4883] tenzih, tesbih[^74] ederek iman ve takvâ ile yarın için çalışmalı, rahmetiyle vaad buyurduğu fevz ü murâda ermelidir.

ELMALILI:59:22-24#6/r1.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:59:22-24#6/r1.speaker: author
ELMALILI:59:22-24#6/r1.claim: Elmalılı says numerous reports attest to the great merit of the final verses of Sūrat al-Hashr.
ELMALILI:59:22-24#6/r1.anchor: bu âyetlerin büyük faziletleri olduğuna dair müte‘addid rivayetler vardır

ELMALILI:59:22-24#6/r2.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:59:22-24#6/r2.speaker: Hazret-i Peygamber
ELMALILI:59:22-24#6/r2.claim: A report from Ma‘qil b. Yasār says that reciting the refuge formula three times in the morning and the final three verses brings 70,000 angels’ prayers until evening; dying that day means martyrdom, and the evening recitation has the same rank.
ELMALILI:59:22-24#6/r2.anchor: Hazret-i Peygamber sallallâhu aleyhi ve sellem buyurmuştur ki: “Her kim sabahleyin üç kere

ELMALILI:59:22-24#6/r3.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:59:22-24#6/r3.speaker: İbn Abbas
ELMALILI:59:22-24#6/r3.claim: Al-Deylemī reports from Ibn Abbas that Allah’s Greatest Name occurs in the final six verses of Sūrat al-Hashr.
ELMALILI:59:22-24#6/r3.anchor: İbn Abbas’tan şöyle rivayet etmiştir: “Allah’ın İsm-i A‘zamı Sûre-i Haşr’ın âhirinde

ELMALILI:59:22-24#6/r4.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:59:22-24#6/r4.speaker: Hazret-i Ali
ELMALILI:59:22-24#6/r4.claim: In a report traced to Muhammad b. Hanefiyye, Ali tells al-Barāʾ to recite the first ten verses of al-Hadīd and the end of al-Hashr before invoking Allah by His Greatest Name, then give the quoted supplication.
ELMALILI:59:22-24#6/r4.anchor: Hazret-i Ali “yâ Berâ!” dedi, “Allah’a İsm-i A‘zam’ı ile dua etmek istersen Sûre-i Hadîd’in evvelinden on âyeti ve Sûre-i Haşr’in âhirini oku

ELMALILI:59:22-24#6/r5.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:59:22-24#6/r5.speaker: Resûlullah
ELMALILI:59:22-24#6/r5.claim: Al-Deylemī transmits from Ali and Ibn Mas‘ūd, as a prophetic report, that the passage beginning with “Law anzalnā” through the end of the sūra is a cure for headache.
ELMALILI:59:22-24#6/r5.anchor: Hazret-i Ali’den ve İbn Mes‘ûd’dan Resûlullah’a merfû‘an “لَوْ أَنزَلْنَا ilâ âhiri’s-sûre rukye-i sudâ‘dır” diye rivayet eylemiştir

ELMALILI:59:22-24#6/r8.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:59:22-24#6/r8.speaker: Abdullah b. Mes‘ûd
ELMALILI:59:22-24#6/r8.claim: Citing al-Sarakhsī’s al-Mabsūṭ, Elmalılı recalls Ibn Mas‘ūd’s teaching that the Qur’an’s main purpose is acting on it, not mere recitation.
ELMALILI:59:22-24#6/r8.anchor: Abdullah b. Mes‘ûd Hazretleri “Kur’ân’ın nüzûlünden asıl maksad mücerred kıraat değil, mûcebince ameldir”

ELMALILI:59:22-24#6/r9.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:59:22-24#6/r9.speaker: author
ELMALILI:59:22-24#6/r9.claim: Reading these healing verses is not for incantation or musical display; one should reflect, gain knowledge and God-fearing, and prepare for tomorrow as 59:18 commands.
ELMALILI:59:22-24#6/r9.anchor: segâhtan makam çatlatmak değil, elini başına koyarak düşünmek ve marifet ile bezenip haşyetullah ile dolarak

ELMALILI:59:22-24#6/r10.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:59:22-24#6/r10.speaker: author
ELMALILI:59:22-24#6/r10.claim: The coming test before the Mighty and Wise God explains why Sūrat al-Hashr is followed by Sūrat al-Mumtaḥina, the test-taking sūra.
ELMALILI:59:22-24#6/r10.anchor: Nitekim bu hikmete mebnî Sûre-i Haşr’i İmtihan Sûresi tâkip edecektir

ELMALILI:59:22-24#6/r11.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:59:22-24#6/r11.speaker: author
ELMALILI:59:22-24#6/r11.claim: Elmalılı closes by praying for forgiveness for believers and their predecessors, hearts free of rancor toward fellow believers, and increased faith and love, dignity, wisdom, and joy through mercy.
ELMALILI:59:22-24#6/r11.anchor: gönüllerimizde mü’min kardeşlerimize karşı hiçbir gıll u gış bırakma, iman ve mahabbetimizi müzdâd, izzetinle i‘zâz, hikmetinle âbâd, rahmetinle dilşâd et

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:59:22/r1.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:59:22/r1.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:59:22/r1.claim: God places the name Allah first, singles out some of His names and attributes, and then reminds readers that the most beautiful names belong to Him.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:59:22/r1.anchor: Cenâb-ı Hak, “Allah” ismini en başa koyarak kendisinin bazı isim ve sıfatlarını özellikle anmakta, ardından en güzel isimlerin kendisine ait olduğunu hatırlatmaktadır

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:59:22/r2.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:59:22/r2.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:59:22/r2.claim: In explaining verse 21's call to God-consciousness, the passage highlights divine unity, limitless knowledge, then expansive mercy and compassion, urging people to approach God first through love, compassion, and forgiveness and treat all creation likewise.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:59:22/r2.anchor: bu âyetlerde bile önce Allah Teâlâ’nın birliğine, sonra ilminin sınırsızlığına, hemen bunların ardından da rahmet ve şefkatinin enginliğine yer verilmesi

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:59:22/r3.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:59:22/r3.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:59:22/r3.claim: Esmāʾ al-ḥusnā means God's names that signify His most beautiful qualities and most perfect meanings.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:59:22/r3.anchor: esmâ-i hüsnâ terimi, “Allah Teâlâ’nın en güzel niteliklerine ve en mükemmel anlamlara delâlet eden isimleri” demektir

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:59:22/r12.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:59:22/r12.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:59:22/r12.claim: Al-Khaliq creates according to His determination.

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:59:22/r13.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:59:22/r13.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:59:22/r13.claim: Al-Bari creates without a prior example and is the source of the fine detail throughout creation.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:59:22/r13.anchor: Bâri’: Örneği olmadan yaratan, yaratmanın bütün evrelerindeki inceliklerin asıl kaynağı

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:59:22/r14.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:59:22/r14.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:59:22/r14.claim: Al-Musawwir determines every sensory and non-sensory, material and spiritual form and characteristic of created things.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:59:22/r14.anchor: Musavvir: Biçim ve özellik veren, yarattıklarının maddî ve mânevî, duyularla algılanan ve algılanamayan bütün şekil ve hususiyetlerini belirleyen

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:59:22/r15.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:59:22/r15.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:59:22/r15.claim: Al-Hakim acts and commands with perfect propriety and possesses judgment and wisdom.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:59:22/r15.anchor: Hakîm: Bütün işleri ve buyrukları yerli yerince olan, hüküm ve hikmet sahibi

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:59:22/r16.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:59:22/r16.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:59:22/r16.claim: The surah closes, as it opened, by saying that all in the heavens and earth glorify God, the Mighty and Wise.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:59:22/r16.anchor: Sûre –ilk âyetinde olduğu gibi– göklerde ve yerde bulunanların hepsinin Allah’ı tesbih ettiği, O’nun azîz ve hakîm olduğu belirtilerek sona ermektedir

QASHANI:59:22-24/r13.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:59:22-24/r13.speaker: author
QASHANI:59:22-24/r13.claim: “The Creator” measures manifestations according to how He wills His names and attributes to appear.
QASHANI:59:22-24/r13.anchor: الخالق } المقدر للمظاهر على حسب ما أراد ظهوره من أسمائه وصفاته

QASHANI:59:22-24/r14.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:59:22-24/r14.speaker: author
QASHANI:59:22-24/r14.claim: “The Maker” differentiates the manifestations through distinct forms within His Essence.
QASHANI:59:22-24/r14.anchor: البارىء } المفصل المميز بعضها عن بعض بالهيئات المتميزة في عين ذاته

QASHANI:59:22-24/r15.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:59:22-24/r15.speaker: author
QASHANI:59:22-24/r15.claim: “The Shaper” gives form to the detailed manifestations of His attributes.

QASHANI:59:22-24/r16.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:59:22-24/r16.speaker: author
QASHANI:59:22-24/r16.claim: The beautiful names appear outwardly in created forms and inwardly in hidden originated forms, praising the Essence through its names and attributes.
QASHANI:59:22-24/r16.anchor: له } هذه { الأسماء الحسنى } الظاهرة في صور المخلوقات المصورة الباطنة في صور المبدعات المغيبة

BIQAI-FULL:v7p545/r1.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v7p545/r1.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v7p545/r1.claim: Ruling requires patience and knowledge of what sustains worldly order; wisdom is knowing why a ruling is required and what brings a good outcome.
BIQAI-FULL:v7p545/r1.anchor: فالحمل على جميع أنواع الصبر والمصابرة ظاهرا بالإيالة العالية هو الحكم والعلم بالأمر الذي لأجله وجب الحكم

BIQAI-FULL:v7p545/r2.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v7p545/r2.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v7p545/r2.claim: Everyone must learn the rulings relevant to them, while a group should study what applies to all, as commanded in the cited verse.
BIQAI-FULL:v7p545/r2.anchor: وأن ينتدب طائفة لعلم ما يعم جميع الناس

BIQAI-FULL:v7p545/r3.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v7p545/r3.speaker: الحرالي
BIQAI-FULL:v7p545/r3.claim: Al-Ḥarālī says wisdom is taught after purification; purification makes one eligible for wisdom, and wisdom eases the burden of legal work.
BIQAI-FULL:v7p545/r3.anchor: فما يعلمهم الحكمة إلا بعد التزكية فمن تزكى فهو من أهلها ومن يترك فليس من أهلها

BIQAI-FULL:v7p545/r4.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v7p545/r4.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v7p545/r4.claim: Wisdom makes difficult obligations easy and transforms the soul’s constriction under law into spaciousness; judgment and wisdom depend on broad knowledge.
BIQAI-FULL:v7p545/r4.anchor: فالحكمة تحلي مرارة جهد العمل بالأحكام فييسر بها ما يعسر دونها

BIQAI-FULL:v7p545/r5.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v7p545/r5.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v7p545/r5.claim: People possess only the knowledge God grants and receive only a corresponding measure of wisdom, as illustrated by Luqmān.
BIQAI-FULL:v7p545/r5.anchor: ولما لم يكن للخلق من العلم إلا بقدر ما يهبهم الله لم يكن لهم من الحكمة إلا مقدار ما يورثهم

BIQAI-FULL:v7p545/r6.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v7p545/r6.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v7p545/r6.claim: Because all knowledge belongs to God, wisdom and judgment truly belong to Him alone; He is al-Ḥakīm and no one else is truly wise.
BIQAI-FULL:v7p545/r6.anchor: فهو الحكيم الذي لا حكيم إلا هو

BIQAI-FULL:v7p545/r7.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v7p545/r7.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v7p545/r7.claim: The names follow without conjunction because no one attribute conveys the whole meaning of Allah; their totality, as revealed and known through His allies, does.
BIQAI-FULL:v7p545/r7.anchor: أتبعه تلك الأوصاف العلى من غير عطف إعلاما بأنه لا شيء منها يؤدي جميع معناه

BIQAI-FULL:v7p545/r8.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v7p545/r8.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v7p545/r8.claim: The names are not apparent opposites requiring conjunction; each name explains the hidden implication of the preceding one, and the passage’s opening and ending embrace each other.
BIQAI-FULL:v7p545/r8.anchor: كل اسم منها كما مضى شارح لما خفي من الذي قبله ومبين للازمه

BIQAI-FULL:v7p545/r9.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v7p545/r9.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v7p545/r9.claim: The cited command to treat Satan as an enemy is linked to steadfastness and high governance.
BIQAI-FULL:v7p545/r9.anchor: أن الشيطان لكم عدو فاتخذوه عدوا

DURR-FULL:v8p123/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v8p123/r1.speaker: الحسن
DURR-FULL:v8p123/r1.claim: Al-Ḥasan reports that one who recites the last three verses of al-Ḥashr in the morning and dies that day, or in the evening and dies that night, is stamped among the martyrs.
DURR-FULL:v8p123/r1.anchor: عن الحسن قال: من قرأ ثلاث آيات من آخر سورة الحشر إذا أصبح فمات من يومه ذلك طبع بطابع الشهداء

DURR-FULL:v8p123/r2.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v8p123/r2.speaker: ابن عباس
DURR-FULL:v8p123/r2.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās reports that God's greatest name occurs in six verses at the end of al-Ḥashr.
DURR-FULL:v8p123/r2.anchor: عن ابن عباس قال: قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم: اسم الله الأعظم في ستة آيات من آخر سورة الحشر

JISHUMI:v9p6863/r10.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v9p6863/r10.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v9p6863/r10.claim: Al-ḥusnā is a superlative meaning the most beautiful of names.
JISHUMI:v9p6863/r10.anchor: والحسنى: اسم تفضيل، بمعنى أحسن الأسماء

JISHUMI:v9p6863/r14.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v9p6863/r14.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v9p6863/r14.claim: Creation is explained as origination according to an exact measure, or as acting without an instrument, or as invention; al-barʾ and al-khalq are near-synonyms.
JISHUMI:v9p6863/r14.anchor: والخلق: الإبداع على تقدير لا ينقص عن مراده، ولا يزيد، وقيل: الخلق أن يفعل لا بآلة

STUDYQURAN:59:22/r1.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:59:22/r1.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:59:22/r1.claim: The passage is called among the “Jewels of the Quran” and is often recited in obligatory and supererogatory prayers.
STUDYQURAN:59:22/r1.anchor: This passage is considered to be among the “Jewels of the Quran”and is often recited in both obligatory and supererogatory prayers.

STUDYQURAN:59:22/r2.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:59:22/r2.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:59:22/r2.claim: The passage gives the Quran's most extensive list of Divine Names: seventeen, or eighteen if the opening pronoun huwa is counted.
STUDYQURAN:59:22/r2.anchor: It provides the most extensive list of Divine Names in the Quran, seventeen in all—or eighteen, if one includes the pronoun He

STUDYQURAN:59:22/r4.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:59:22/r4.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:59:22/r4.claim: Sayings extol recitation of the sūrah's final three verses, sometimes including 59:21.
STUDYQURAN:59:22/r4.anchor: Many sayings extol the recitation of this sūrah, especially these last three verses (sometimes including v. 21 as well).

STUDYQURAN:59:22/r22.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:59:22/r22.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:59:22/r22.claim: Creator, Maker, and Fashioner describe stages of creation: measuring before existence, bringing into being, then giving form and characteristics.
STUDYQURAN:59:22/r22.anchor: The Creator indicates the Quality of God through which He measures things out before they come into existence in this world; the Maker

STUDYQURAN:59:22/r23.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:59:22/r23.speaker: Q
STUDYQURAN:59:22/r23.claim: Alternatively, the three Names refer to stages through which creatures, especially humans, develop in the womb.
STUDYQURAN:59:22/r23.anchor: these three Divine Names can be seen as referring more specifically to the three stages through which creatures, in particular human beings, develop in the womb (Q).

STUDYQURAN:59:22/r24.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:59:22/r24.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:59:22/r24.claim: The wording “unto Him belong the Most Beautiful Names” is linked with 7:180, 17:110, and 20:8.
STUDYQURAN:59:22/r24.anchor: Regarding unto Him belong the Most Beautiful Names (cf. 7:180; 17:110; 20:8)

STUDYQURAN:59:22/r25.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:59:22/r25.speaker: ḥadīth
STUDYQURAN:59:22/r25.claim: A famous ḥadīth says God has ninety-nine Names and whoever enumerates them will enter the Garden.
STUDYQURAN:59:22/r25.anchor: a famous ḥadīth states, “God has ninety-nine Names—one hundred minus one—and whosoever enumerates them will enter the Garden” (IK)

STUDYQURAN:59:22/r26.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:59:22/r26.speaker: many scholars
STUDYQURAN:59:22/r26.claim: Many scholars hold that God has more than ninety-nine Names, many unrevealed to humans.
STUDYQURAN:59:22/r26.anchor: though many scholars maintain that God has more than ninety-nine Names, many of which are not revealed to human beings.

STUDYQURAN:59:22/r27.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:59:22/r27.speaker: the Prophet
STUDYQURAN:59:22/r27.claim: The Prophet is reported to invoke God by every Name He has used for Himself, revealed in Scripture, taught to creation, or kept in unseen knowledge.
STUDYQURAN:59:22/r27.anchor: the Prophet is reported to have called upon God saying, “I implore Thee by every Name that is Thine

TABATABAI:59:21-23/r3.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:59:21-23/r3.speaker: author
TABATABAI:59:21-23/r3.claim: The next three verses list some beautiful divine names and declare God's transcendence; joined to the command to remember, they teach worshippers to invoke those names and recognize their own corresponding deficiencies.
TABATABAI:59:21-23/r3.anchor: هذه الآية والآيتان بعدها وإن كانت مسوقة لتعداد قبيل من أسمائه تعالى الحسنى والإشارة إلى تسميته تعالى بكل اسم أحسن

TABATABAI:59:21-23/r4.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:59:21-23/r4.speaker: author
TABATABAI:59:21-23/r4.claim: Together with the mountain's collapse from fear of God, these names explain its awe: He alone is God, knowing the unseen and seen, as the following names further describe.
TABATABAI:59:21-23/r4.anchor: وبانضمامها إلى الآية السابقة وما فيها من قوله { من خشية الله } تفيد تعليل خشوع الجبل وتصدعه من خشية الله

NAHHAS:v4p406/r6.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v4p406/r6.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v4p406/r6.claim: خلق can mean measured or determined, as attested by a poetic use of خلقت.
NAHHAS:v4p406/r6.anchor: معنى خلق الشيء قدره كما قال ( ولأنت تفري ما خلقت وبعض … القوم يخلق ثم لا يفري )

NAHHAS:v4p406/r7.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v4p406/r7.speaker: محمد بن إبراهيم بن عرفة
NAHHAS:v4p406/r7.claim: Ibn ʿUrafa defines God's creating as determining and originating without a prior model, addition, or subtraction; al-Nahhas connects this sense to البارئ.
NAHHAS:v4p406/r7.anchor: محمد بن إبراهيم بن عرفة قال معنى خلق الله الشيء قدره مخترعا على غير أصل بلا زيادة ولا نقصان

NAHHAS:v4p406/r8.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v4p406/r8.speaker: قيل
NAHHAS:v4p406/r8.claim: One view equates البارئ with الخالق; al-Nahhas calls this loose usage, perhaps excusable because الخالق comes immediately before it.
NAHHAS:v4p406/r8.anchor: قيل معنى البارىء الخالق وهذا فيه تساهل لضعف من يقوله في العربية أو على أن يتساهل فيه لأنه قبله الخالق

NAHHAS:v4p406/r9.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v4p406/r9.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v4p406/r9.claim: Al-Nahhas says برأ الله الخلق means He proportioned and adjusted them; this distinguishes it from the preceding act of measuring.
NAHHAS:v4p406/r9.anchor: وحقيقة هذا أن معنى برأ الله الخلق سواهم وعدلهم ألا ترى اتساق الكلام أن قبله خلق أي قدر وبعده برى أي عدل وسوى

NAHHAS:v4p406/r10.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v4p406/r10.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v4p406/r10.claim: المصور follows measuring and proportioning by giving creatures an image or form.

NAHHAS:v4p406/r11.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v4p406/r11.speaker: قيل
NAHHAS:v4p406/r11.claim: Another proposed derivation links المصور to صار يصير; al-Nahhas rejects it because that form would use ياء, and instead derives it from الصورة, the model or form.
NAHHAS:v4p406/r11.anchor: وقد قيل أن المصور مشتق من صار يصير ولو كان كذا لكان بالياء ولكنه مشتق من الصورة وهي المثال

NAHHAS:v4p406/r12.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v4p406/r12.speaker: أبو هريرة
NAHHAS:v4p406/r12.claim: Abu Hurayra reports from the Prophet that God has ninety-nine names.
NAHHAS:v4p406/r12.anchor: قال أبو هريرة عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم لله تسعة وتسعون اسما

NAHHAS:v4p406/r13.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v4p406/r13.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v4p406/r13.claim: All creation glorifies God by showing that it has a maker and manager with no equal; its very form declares Him free of likeness.
NAHHAS:v4p406/r13.anchor: لأنه دال على أن له محدثا ومدبرا لا نظير له فقد صار بهيئته يسبح لله أي منزها له عن الأشياء

NAHHAS:v4p406/r14.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v4p406/r14.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v4p406/r14.claim: العزيز describes God's power to take vengeance on those who disbelieve in Him.
NAHHAS:v4p406/r14.anchor: ( وهو العزيز ) أي في انتقامه ممن كفر به

NAHHAS:v4p406/r15.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v4p406/r15.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v4p406/r15.claim: الحكيم describes God's acts as free of flaw; another reported sense is الحاكم, “ruler/judge.”
NAHHAS:v4p406/r15.anchor: ( الحكيم ) فيما خلقه لأن حكمته لا يرى فيها خلل وقيل الحكيم بمعنى الحاكم

SAMIN-DURR:59:24/r1.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:59:24/r1.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:59:24/r1.claim: The common reading has kasra on و and nominative ر, making المصور either an adjective or predicate.
SAMIN-DURR:59:24/r1.anchor: العامة على كسر الواو ورفع الراء: إما صفة، وإما خبرا

SAMIN-DURR:59:24/r2.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:59:24/r2.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:59:24/r2.claim: Ali, al-Hasan, Ibn al-Sumayfa, and Hatib read فتح الواو and accusative ر; المصور is governed by الباري and refers to Adam or Adam and his descendants.
SAMIN-DURR:59:24/r2.anchor: وقرأ أمير المؤمنين علي بن أبي طالب والحسن وابن السميفع وحاطب بن أبي بلتعة بفتح الواو ونصب الراء

SAMIN-DURR:59:24/r3.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:59:24/r3.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:59:24/r3.claim: On the accusative reading one must connect المصور to الباري and not pause after it, lest the case be misread.
SAMIN-DURR:59:24/r3.anchor: وعلى هذه القراءة يحرم الوقف على " المصور " بل يجب الوصل ليظهر النصب في الراء

SAMIN-DURR:59:24/r4.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:59:24/r4.speaker: أمير المؤمنين
SAMIN-DURR:59:24/r4.claim: A report from Ali also has open و and genitive ر; it keeps the meaning but makes the active participle govern its object by annexation for lightness.
SAMIN-DURR:59:24/r4.anchor: وروي عن أمير المؤمنين أيضا فتح الواو وجر الراء. وهي كالأولى في المعنى

SAMIN-DURR:59:24/r5.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:59:24/r5.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:59:24/r5.claim: The genitive reading also forbids pausing at المصور.
SAMIN-DURR:59:24/r5.anchor: والوقف على المصور في هذه القراءة أيضا حرام. وقد نبه عليه بعضهم

SAMIN-DURR:59:24/r6.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:59:24/r6.speaker: مكي
SAMIN-DURR:59:24/r6.claim: Makki allows accusative المصور with open و, governed by الباري, referring to Adam and his descendants; al-Samin notes this reading had already been reported.
SAMIN-DURR:59:24/r6.anchor: وقال مكي: " ويجوز نصبه في الكلام، ولا بد من فتح الواو

SAMIN-DURR:59:24/r7.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:59:24/r7.speaker: مكي
SAMIN-DURR:59:24/r7.claim: Makki rejects accusative with kasra و because it would be a divine attribute governed by the preceding active participle; al-Samin parses a confirmed report as a detached accusative of praise.
SAMIN-DURR:59:24/r7.anchor: وقال أيضا: " ولا يجوز نصبه مع كسر الواو، ويروى عن علي رضي الله عنه "

SAMIN-DURR:59:24/r8.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:59:24/r8.speaker: مكي
SAMIN-DURR:59:24/r8.claim: Makki derives المصور from صور يصور, not صار يصير, which would require المصير and does not fit the meaning.
SAMIN-DURR:59:24/r8.anchor: والمصور: مفعل من صور يصور، ولا يحسن أن يكون من صار يصير

ZAJJAJ:v5p150#2/r8.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v5p150#2/r8.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v5p150#2/r8.claim: A transmitted accusative reading al-bāriʾa al-muṣawwira should not be read; it would mean “the one who originated Adam and formed him.”
ZAJJAJ:v5p150#2/r8.anchor: وقد رويت رواية لا ينبغي أن تقرأ، رويت (البارئ المصور) بالنصب معناه الذي برأ آدم وصورة

ZAJJAJ:v5p151/r1.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v5p151/r1.speaker: التفسير
ZAJJAJ:v5p151/r1.claim: Exegetical reports say God has ninety-nine names and whoever enumerates them enters Paradise; another identifies “Allah” as the greatest name.
ZAJJAJ:v5p151/r1.anchor: جاء في التفسير أنها تسعة وتسعون اسما، من أحصاها دخل الجنة

ZAJJAJ:v5p151/r2.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v5p151/r2.speaker: أبو هريرة الدوسي
ZAJJAJ:v5p151/r2.claim: Abu Hurayra reports from the Prophet that God has one hundred names less one; whoever enumerates them enters Paradise, followed by a list of names.
ZAJJAJ:v5p151/r2.anchor: روى أبو هريرة الدوسي عن النبي عليه السلام قال إن لله مائة اسم غير واحد من أحصاها دخل الجنة.

ZAJJAJ:v5p151/r3.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v5p151/r3.speaker: سيبويه
ZAJJAJ:v5p151/r3.claim: Sibawayh says al-Khalil proposed that Allah derives from ilāh, with the definite article replacing the hamza.
ZAJJAJ:v5p151/r3.anchor: قال سيبويه: سألت الخليل عن هذا الاسم فقال: الأصل فيه إله فأدخلت الألف واللام بدلا من الهمزة.

ZAJJAJ:v5p151/r4.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v5p151/r4.speaker: الخليل
ZAJJAJ:v5p151/r4.claim: Al-Khalil also proposed that the original form was lāh, with the definite article added as an inseparable prefix.
ZAJJAJ:v5p151/r4.anchor: وقال مرة أخرى: الأصل لاه وأدخلت الألف واللام لازمة.

ZAJJAJ:v5p151/r5.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v5p151/r5.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v5p151/r5.claim: Al-Raḥmān is exclusive to God, means abundantly merciful, and uses an intensive faʿlān form like “full” or “sated.”
ZAJJAJ:v5p151/r5.anchor: وأما الرحمن الرحيم فالرحمن اسم الله خاصة لا يقال لغير الله رحمن، ومعناه المبالغ في الرحمة وأرحم الراحمين

ZAJJAJ:v5p151/r6.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v5p151/r6.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v5p151/r6.claim: Al-Raḥīm is the active participle of raḥima and also conveys intensity.
ZAJJAJ:v5p151/r6.anchor: والرحيم اسم الفاعل من رحم فهو رحيم، وهو أيضا للمبالغة والأحد أصله الوحد

ZAJJAJ:v5p151/r7.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v5p151/r7.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v5p151/r7.claim: Al-Aḥad comes from al-waḥd, “the one,” who has no likeness.
ZAJJAJ:v5p151/r7.anchor: والأحد أصله الوحد بمعنى الواحد، وهو الواحد الذي ليس كمثله شيء. والصمد السيد

ZAJJAJ:v5p151/r8.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v5p151/r8.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v5p151/r8.claim: Al-Ṣamad is the master toward whom all things turn; their turning to God is shown by His workmanship in everything.
ZAJJAJ:v5p151/r8.anchor: والصمد السيد الذي صمد له كل شيء، أي قصد قصده. وتأويل صمود كل شيء لله أن في كل شيء أثر صنعة الله.

ASAD-NOTES:59:24/r1.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:59:24/r1.speaker: author
ASAD-NOTES:59:24/r1.claim: God is Creator, Maker and Shaper of all forms and appearances.
ASAD-NOTES:59:24/r1.anchor: He is God, the Creator, the Maker who shapes all forms and appearances

ASAD-NOTES:59:24/r2.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:59:24/r2.speaker: author
ASAD-NOTES:59:24/r2.claim: The attributes of perfection belong to God alone, and all creation glorifies Him as almighty and wise.
ASAD-NOTES:59:24/r2.anchor: His [alone] are the attributes of perfection

ASAD-NOTES:59:24#n31/r1.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:59:24#n31/r1.speaker: Baydawi
ASAD-NOTES:59:24#n31/r1.claim: Baydawi treats al-bari' (Maker) and al-musawwir (Shaper of forms and appearances) as one unit here.
ASAD-NOTES:59:24#n31/r1.anchor: evidently constitute here one single unit

ASAD-NOTES:59:24#n32/r1.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:59:24#n32/r1.speaker: author
ASAD-NOTES:59:24#n32/r1.claim: For the rendering of al-asma' al-husna as attributes of perfection, Asad refers to his note on 7:180.
ASAD-NOTES:59:24#n32/r1.anchor: For this rendering of al-asma' al-husna, see surah 7, note 145

BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p583/r1.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p583/r1.speaker: author
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p583/r1.claim: Bint al-Shati finds the gloss Creator plausible; al-Tabari likewise glosses al-Bari as your Creator and relates it to God bringing creation into being.
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p583/r1.anchor: وتفسير البارئ فى المسألة، بالخالق يبدو قريبا. وقاله الطبرى فى تأويله: أي إلى خالقكم

BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p583/r2.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p583/r2.speaker: الراغب
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p583/r2.claim: Al-Raghib says al-Bari is a designation specially applied to God.
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p583/r2.anchor: ذكر الراغب أن " البارئ: خُصَّ بوصفه تعالى

BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p583/r3.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p583/r3.speaker: الزمخشري
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p583/r3.claim: Al-Zamakhshari distinguishes the Creator, who determines what will be brought into being, from al-Bari, who differentiates forms; Abu Hayyan gives the same account.
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p583/r3.anchor: الخالق، المقدر لما يوجده، البارئ: المميز بعضه عن بعض بالأشكال المختلفة. ومثله فى (البحر المحيط) لأبي حيان

BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p583/r4.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p583/r4.speaker: ابن الأثير
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p583/r4.claim: Ibn al-Athir says al-Bari creates without a prior model and is used especially for creating animals, only rarely for other created things.
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p583/r4.anchor: البارئ. وهو الذى خلق الخلق لاعن مثال. ولهذه اللفظة من الاختصاص بخلق الحيوان، ما ليس لها بغيره من المخلوقات

BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p583/r5.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p583/r5.speaker: author
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p583/r5.claim: Bint al-Shati favors Ibn al-Athir's distinction: creation is comprehensive, while al-Bari is generally associated with living beings; Quranic usage supports the distinction across human groups and animal creation.
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p583/r5.anchor: وهذا الوجه الدقيق من التمييز بين الخالق والبارئ هو ما يؤنس إليه استقراء ما فى القرآن من آياتهما، وتدبر سياقها: فالخلق شامل لكل شيء

BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p583/r6.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p583/r6.speaker: author
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p583/r6.claim: The verb baraʾ is also used for nonliving things in 57:22, so Ibn al-Athir carefully says it is rarely, rather than never, used beyond animals.
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p583/r6.anchor: لكن آية الحديد، يتعلق فيها الفعل " نبرأها " بـ (ما أصاب من مصيبة فى الأرض ولا فى أنفسكم)

BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p582/r2.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p582/r2.speaker: author
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p582/r2.claim: The noun appears twice in 2:54 and as one of God's beautiful names in 59:24; its verb occurs in 57:22, while the unhamzated bariyya appears in 98:6–7.
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p582/r2.anchor: وجاء البارئ اسما من أسماء الله تعالى الحسنى فى آية الحشر 24

BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p582/r3.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p582/r3.speaker: ابن فارس
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p582/r3.claim: Ibn Faris gives the root two principles: creation and separation or distance from something; barāʾa and tabarruʾ belong to the latter.
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p582/r3.anchor: ومادة (برأ) فى مقاييس اللغة أصلان إليهما ترجع فروع الباب

NASHR:v2p38/r4.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v2p38/r4.speaker: author
NASHR:v2p38/r4.claim: For al-Dūrī's transmission from al-Kisāʾī, most Maghribī authorities report imāla on al-bāriʾ al-muṣawwir, treating it like bāriʾukum; Ibn Farḥ's route also reports imāla.
NASHR:v2p38/r4.anchor: واختلف عنه في: البارئ المصور من سورة الحشر فروى عنه إمالته، وأجراه مجرى بارئكم

NASHR:v2p38/r5.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v2p38/r5.speaker: أبو عثمان الضرير
NASHR:v2p38/r5.claim: Abū ʿUthmān al-Ḍarīr reports fatḥ for al-bāriʾ al-muṣawwir, as do most reading sources.
NASHR:v2p38/r5.anchor: ورواه عنه بالفتح خصوصا أبو عثمان الضرير وهو الذي في أكثر القراءات

ALUSI-FULL:v28p64/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v28p64/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v28p64/r1.claim: Al-Khāliq is explained either as determining things according to wisdom or originating them without prior material or model; creation can also mean producing one thing from another.

ALUSI-FULL:v28p64/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v28p64/r2.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v28p64/r2.claim: Al-Bāriʾ brings things into existence free from discrepancy, as wisdom and their nature require; it can also mean distinguishing them by differing forms.
ALUSI-FULL:v28p64/r2.anchor: الموجد لها بريئة من تفاوت ما تقتضيه بحسب الحكمة والجبلة

ALUSI-FULL:v28p64/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v28p64/r3.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v28p64/r3.claim: Al-Muṣawwir brings each thing’s form and qualities into existence as He wills.

ALUSI-FULL:v28p64/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v28p64/r4.speaker: الراغب
ALUSI-FULL:v28p64/r4.claim: Al-Raghib defines image as the form by which entities are imprinted and distinguished, either sensible to common people and specialists or intellectual, apprehended only by specialists.
ALUSI-FULL:v28p64/r4.anchor: الصورة ما تنتقش بها الأعيان وتتميز بها عن غيرها

ALUSI-FULL:v28p64/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v28p64/r5.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v28p64/r5.claim: Al-Raghib links these two kinds of form to ‘We created you, then fashioned you’ and other verses.

ALUSI-FULL:v28p64/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v28p64/r6.speaker: علي وحاطب بن أبي بلتعة والحسن وابن السمقيع
ALUSI-FULL:v28p64/r6.claim: Ali, Hatib ibn Abi Baltaʿa, Hasan, and Ibn al-Sumayqiʿ read المصور with fatḥa on the wāw and in the accusative, as an object of al-Bāriʾ, meaning the genus of image-makers.
ALUSI-FULL:v28p64/r6.anchor: ابن السمقيع ( المصور ) بفتح الواو والنصب

ALUSI-FULL:v28p64/r7.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v28p64/r7.speaker: علي
ALUSI-FULL:v28p64/r7.claim: Ali also read المصور with fatḥa on the wāw and kasra on the rāʾ, as a construct phrase with the object, like the one striking the boy.
ALUSI-FULL:v28p64/r7.anchor: وعن علي كرم الله تعالى وجهه فتح الواو وكسر الراء

ALUSI-FULL:v28p64/r8.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v28p64/r8.speaker: الخانية
ALUSI-FULL:v28p64/r8.claim: Al-Khāniyya says that reading المصور with fatḥa on the wāw invalidates prayer; al-Alusi allows this if it is construed as an attribute of God and otherwise questions the ruling.
ALUSI-FULL:v28p64/r8.anchor: بفتح الواو هنا تفسد الصلاة ولعله أراد

ALUSI-FULL:v28p64/r9.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v28p64/r9.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v28p64/r9.claim: The most beautiful names denote the finest meanings.
ALUSI-FULL:v28p64/r9.anchor: له الأسماء الحسنى ( الدالة على محاسن المعاني

ALUSI-FULL:v28p64/r10.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v28p64/r10.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v28p64/r10.claim: All beings glorify God by the language of their state, through the wisdoms and benefits in them, or by actual speech in a manner suited to each, as many mystics hold.
ALUSI-FULL:v28p64/r10.anchor: من الموجودات بلسان الحال لما تضمنته من الحكم والمصالح

ALUSI-FULL:v28p64/r11.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v28p64/r11.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v28p64/r11.claim: The two names gather all perfections: al-Aziz signals perfect power as the overpowering, and al-Hakim signals perfect knowledge through action according to wisdom.
ALUSI-FULL:v28p64/r11.anchor: الجامع للكمالات كافة فإنها مع تكثرها وتشعبها راجعة إلى كمال القدرة

ALUSI-FULL:v28p64/r12.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v28p64/r12.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v28p64/r12.claim: The ending suggests adorning with divine perfections after declaring God incomparable, as in 42:11.

ALUSI-FULL:v28p64/r13.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v28p64/r13.speaker: النبي صلى الله تعالى عليه وسلم عن معقل بن يسار
ALUSI-FULL:v28p64/r13.claim: Whoever says the seeking-refuge formula three times morning or evening and reads the last three verses of al-Hashr has 70,000 angels pray for him until the opposite time; if he dies that day or night, he dies a martyr. Al-Tirmidhi graded the report hasan.
ALUSI-FULL:v28p64/r13.anchor: عن معقل بن يسار عن النبي صلى الله تعالى عليه وسلم

ALUSI-FULL:v28p64#2/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v28p64#2/r1.speaker: النبي صلى الله تعالى عليه وسلم عن ابن عباس
ALUSI-FULL:v28p64#2/r1.claim: A report from Ibn Abbas says that God’s greatest name occurs in the six final verses of al-Hashr.
ALUSI-FULL:v28p64#2/r1.anchor: عن ابن عباس مرفوعا اسم الله الأعظم في ست آيات

ALUSI-FULL:v28p64#2/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v28p64#2/r2.speaker: علي عن البراء بن عازب
ALUSI-FULL:v28p64#2/r2.claim: Al-Bara asked Ali for the prayer taught to him by the Prophet through Gabriel; Ali prescribed the first ten verses of al-Hadid, the end of al-Hashr, and an invocation beginning ‘O One who is thus.’
ALUSI-FULL:v28p64#2/r2.anchor: قال لعليابن أبي طالب كرم الله تعالى وجهه

BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p88#2/r1.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p88#2/r1.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p88#2/r1.claim: Al-Khāliq determines and directs a thing by planning from one state to another.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p88#2/r1.anchor: المقدر والمقلب للشيء بالتدبير إلى غيره، كما قال:

BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p88#2/r2.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p88#2/r2.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p88#2/r2.claim: Al-Bāriʾ brings entities from nonexistence into existence.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p88#2/r2.anchor: المنشئ للأعيان من العدم إلى الوجود

BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p88#2/r3.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p88#2/r3.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p88#2/r3.claim: Al-Muṣawwir gives creatures distinguishing forms; ṣūrah can mean an exemplar.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p88#2/r3.anchor: الممثل للمخلوقات بالعلامات التي يتميز بعضها عن بعض

BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p88#2/r4.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p88#2/r4.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p88#2/r4.claim: The sequence is creation, bringing into being, then shaping.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p88#2/r4.anchor: فأولا يكون خلقا ثم برءا ثم تصويرا.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p88#2/r5.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p88#2/r5.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p88#2/r5.claim: Maʿqil ibn Yasār reports the Prophet prescribed the refuge formula three times morning or evening and the last three verses of al-Ḥashr; 70,000 angels pray for the reciter until evening, and death that day brings martyrdom, with the same rank for evening recitation.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p88#2/r5.anchor: عن معقل بن يسار أن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم قال:

BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p88#2/r6.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p88#2/r6.speaker: أبو عيسى
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p88#2/r6.claim: Abū ʿĪsā calls the report gharīb, known only through this route.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p88#2/r6.anchor: هذا حديث غريب لا نعرفه إلا من هذا الوجه

BAYDAWI-FULL:59:23-24/r8.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:59:23-24/r8.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:59:23-24/r8.claim: Al-Khāliq is the one who measures things according to the demands of His wisdom.

BAYDAWI-FULL:59:23-24/r9.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:59:23-24/r9.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:59:23-24/r9.claim: Al-Bāriʾ brings things into existence free of disproportion.

BAYDAWI-FULL:59:23-24/r10.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:59:23-24/r10.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:59:23-24/r10.claim: Al-Muṣawwir brings things' forms and qualities into existence as He wills.

BAYDAWI-FULL:59:23-24/r11.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:59:23-24/r11.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:59:23-24/r11.claim: God's names are beautiful because they indicate meanings of excellence.

BAYDAWI-FULL:59:23-24/r12.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:59:23-24/r12.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:59:23-24/r12.claim: Everything in the heavens and earth glorifies Him because He is transcendent of all deficiencies.

BAYDAWI-FULL:59:23-24/r13.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:59:23-24/r13.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:59:23-24/r13.claim: These names encompass all perfections, which return to perfection in power and knowledge.
BAYDAWI-FULL:59:23-24/r13.anchor: الجامع للكمالات بأسرها فإنها راجعة إلى الكمال في القدرة والعلم

BAYDAWI-FULL:59:23-24/r14.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:59:23-24/r14.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
BAYDAWI-FULL:59:23-24/r14.claim: A report from the Prophet promises forgiveness of past and future sins to whoever recites Sūrat al-Ḥashr; no grading is stated.
BAYDAWI-FULL:59:23-24/r14.anchor: من قرأ سورة الحشر غفر الله له ما تقدم من ذنبه

BIQAI-FULL:v7p541/r13.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v7p541/r13.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v7p541/r13.claim: The proof of oneness from God's majesty concludes, then a second proof begins by moving through levels from the hiddenest to the hidden and then the manifest.
BIQAI-FULL:v7p541/r13.anchor: ولما تم دليل الوحدانية بما حل من التفهيم بالتدني إلى الملك ثم بالتعلي إلى التكبر فأنتج هذه الخاتمة

BIQAI-FULL:v7p541/r14.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v7p541/r14.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v7p541/r14.claim: The new proof starts with faith in the unseen; leaving that ground leads to ruin.
BIQAI-FULL:v7p541/r14.anchor: إعلاما بأنه لا براح عن الإيمان بالغيب , ومن برح عنه هلك

BIQAI-FULL:v7p541/r15.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v7p541/r15.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v7p541/r15.claim: No one but God truly merits the pronoun: He exists through Himself, whereas every other possible being might not exist.
BIQAI-FULL:v7p541/r15.anchor: أي الذي لا شيء يستحق أن يطلق عليه هذا الضمير غيره لأن وجوده من ذاته ولا شيء غيره إلا وهو ممكن

BIQAI-FULL:v7p541/r16.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v7p541/r16.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v7p541/r16.claim: Allah is the most familiar, true name with no namesake and no equal.
BIQAI-FULL:v7p541/r16.anchor: الذي ليس له سمي فلا كفوء له

BIQAI-FULL:v7p541/r17.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v7p541/r17.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v7p541/r17.claim: The author begins a proof from creation: the true creator assigns each thing its measure, like a shoemaker marking a boundary and size on leather before cutting and shaping it.
BIQAI-FULL:v7p541/r17.anchor: كالحاذي يخلق أي يقدر في الجلد حدا وقدرا لنعل ونحوه

BIQAI-FULL:v7p542/r1.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v7p542/r1.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v7p542/r1.claim: True creation includes complete estimation and separation: God alone encompasses every limit and can restore what creatures cannot reassemble, as successive prenatal creation illustrates.
BIQAI-FULL:v7p542/r1.anchor: فلا يملك الخلق والفرق إلا من يملك الجميع والرب

BIQAI-FULL:v7p542/r2.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v7p542/r2.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v7p542/r2.claim: Calling creatures creators is a potentially misleading appearance: all creation, including acts in the visible and unseen realms, belongs to God. This grounds tawhid and the community's faith; al-Qadariyya are called this community's Magi.
BIQAI-FULL:v7p542/r2.anchor: وتلايح تحت هذا اللبس في إطلاق اسم الخالق على الخالق الحق ذي الحول والقوة والقدرة والإحاطة

BIQAI-FULL:v7p542/r3.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v7p542/r3.speaker: شاعرهم
BIQAI-FULL:v7p542/r3.claim: The cited poet distinguishes making something from completing it: some people create or estimate, then fail to carry the work through; the line witnesses تفري.
BIQAI-FULL:v7p542/r3.anchor: كما قال شاعرهم : ولأنت تفري ما خلقت وبعض القوم يخلق ثم لا يفري

BIQAI-FULL:v7p542/r4.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v7p542/r4.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v7p542/r4.claim: Al-Bāriʾ refines, separates, and repairs what was estimated so it can receive its form; full knowledge yields exact preparation, while limited makers leave defects that may thwart the intended result.
BIQAI-FULL:v7p542/r4.anchor: { البارئ } أي الذي يدقق بما وقع به التقدير ويقطعه ويصلحه لقبول الصورة على أتم حال

BIQAI-FULL:v7p542/r5.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v7p542/r5.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v7p542/r5.claim: Al-Muṣawwir completes visible detail, plan, and bodily parts; beyond outward form comes only the subtle maturation of an enlivened creature toward its appointed perfection.
BIQAI-FULL:v7p542/r5.anchor: التصوير إتمام تفصيل الخلق الظاهر وإكمال تخطيطه وإحكام أعضائه

BIQAI-FULL:v7p542/r6.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v7p542/r6.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v7p542/r6.claim: A building illustrates the names' stages: an engineer estimates the plan, craftsmen prepare stone and timber, and builders assemble the form; only God fashions with full wisdom and perfection.
BIQAI-FULL:v7p542/r6.anchor: ويتضح الفرق جدا بين الأسماء الثلاثة بالبناء فإنه يحتاج أولا إلى مقدر يقدر ما لا بد منه

BIQAI-FULL:v7p544/r1.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v7p544/r1.speaker: الرازي
BIQAI-FULL:v7p544/r1.claim: Al-Rāzī says fashioning reaches every part of the world, even an atom, an ant, and each ant's organs; its intricate structure and wisdom point to its fashioner.
BIQAI-FULL:v7p544/r1.anchor: قال الرازي في اللوامع : والتصير موجود في كل أجزاء العالم وإن صغر حتى في الذرة والنملة

BIQAI-FULL:v7p544/r2.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v7p544/r2.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v7p544/r2.claim: The beautiful names belong exclusively to God, including the wisdom necessary for fashioning; human beings cannot apprehend Him fully.
BIQAI-FULL:v7p544/r2.anchor: قوله تعالى : { له } أي خاصة لا لغيره { الأسماء الحسنى } اي من الحكيم

BIQAI-FULL:v7p544/r3.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v7p544/r3.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v7p544/r3.claim: The imperfect verb signals that God's creatures continually renew their glorification, a reminder to deficient beings of His abiding perfection.
BIQAI-FULL:v7p544/r3.anchor: دل على دوام اتصافه بذلك من يحتاج لما له من النقص من الخلق إلى التذكير فعبر بالمضارع

BIQAI-FULL:v7p544/r4.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v7p544/r4.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v7p544/r4.claim: The construction with لَهُ conveys exclusive glorification of God through the object restriction and the preposition lā m.
BIQAI-FULL:v7p544/r4.anchor: على وجه التخصيص بما أفهمه قصر المتعدي وتعديته باللام

BIQAI-FULL:v7p544/r5.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v7p544/r5.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v7p544/r5.claim: He omits ما before الأرض and joins it directly to heaven, hinting that earth shares heaven's elevation as evidence of God's perfection, like one entity.
BIQAI-FULL:v7p544/r5.anchor: كالشيء الواحدج بإسقاط ( ما ) وألصقها بها إلاحة إلى ذلك

BIQAI-FULL:v7p544/r6.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v7p544/r6.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v7p544/r6.claim: Al-ʿAzīz is the One who overcomes everything, has no equal, is difficult to reach, and is urgently needed.
BIQAI-FULL:v7p544/r6.anchor: العزيز } أي الذي يغلب كل شيء ولا يغلبه شيء ولا يوجد له مثل

BIQAI-FULL:v7p544/r7.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v7p544/r7.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v7p544/r7.claim: Wisdom is perfected judgment brought to a firm conclusion that cannot be overturned.
BIQAI-FULL:v7p544/r7.anchor: من الحكمة وهي إتقان الحكم وإنهاؤها إلى جد لا يمكن نقضه

BIQAI-FULL:v7p544/r8.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v7p544/r8.speaker: الحرالي
BIQAI-FULL:v7p544/r8.claim: Al-Ḥarālī defines judgment as restraining and directing someone for their good: it appears forceful but is inwardly gentle, disliked at first yet yielding later satisfaction and relief.
BIQAI-FULL:v7p544/r8.anchor: قال الحرالي : المنع عما يترامى إليه المحكوم إيالة عليه وحمله على ما يمتنع منه نظرا له

BIQAI-FULL:v7p544/r9.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v7p544/r9.speaker: الحرالي
BIQAI-FULL:v7p544/r9.claim: Al-Ḥarālī illustrates bodily judgment as medical treatment, citing the instruction to seek treatment and that God sent a remedy with illness; no grading or source is stated.
BIQAI-FULL:v7p544/r9.anchor: فموقعه في الأبدان المداواة ( تداووا عباد الله فإن الذي أنزل الداء أنزل الدواء )

BIQAI-FULL:v7p544/r10.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v7p544/r10.speaker: الحرالي
BIQAI-FULL:v7p544/r10.claim: Al-Ḥarālī applies judgment in religion to obeying rulings, patient striving, and confronting outward enemies and inward enemies such as the self, family, and Satan.
BIQAI-FULL:v7p544/r10.anchor: وموقعه ف الأديان التزام الأحكام والصبر والمصابرة على مجاهدة الأعمال

IBNASHUR-FULL:v28p64/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v28p64/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v28p64/r1.claim: The sūrah presents the Qurʾān’s greatness and its power to humble its adherents, and closes with divine attributes and universal glorification that commend believers and allude reproachfully to disbelievers.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v28p64/r1.anchor: وبيان عظمة القرآن وجلالته واقتضائه خشوع أهله

IBNASHUR-FULL:v28p64/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v28p64/r2.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v28p64/r2.claim: Its discussion also signals the wisdom of Islamic rules for transferring wealth among Muslims without burdening its owners and urges obedience to what God legislates through His Messenger.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v28p64/r2.anchor: وتخلل ذلك إيماء إلى حكمة شرائع انتقال الأموال بين المسلمين

IBNASHUR-FULL:v28p64/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v28p64/r3.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v28p64/r3.claim: The sūrah’s closing declaration that all in heaven and earth glorify God praises believers and implicitly reproaches disbelievers.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v28p64/r3.anchor: وختمت بصفات عظيمة من الصفات الإلاهية وأنه { يسبح له ما في السماوات والأرض }

IBNASHUR-FULL:v28p123/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v28p123/r2.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v28p123/r2.claim: The opening “He” and repetition of the clause follow the same analysis as the preceding verse; if it is a pronoun of matter, the following sentence predicates it.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v28p123/r2.anchor: القول في ضمير { هو } المفتتح به وفي تكرير الجملة

IBNASHUR-FULL:v28p123/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v28p123/r3.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v28p123/r3.claim: Definiteness in both parts restricts the statement to God as Creator rather than the alleged partners, refuting the divinity of what cannot create; Ibn ʿAshur cites 16:20 and 16:17.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v28p123/r3.anchor: وجملة { الله الخالق } تفيد قصرا بطريق تعريف جزأي الجملة

IBNASHUR-FULL:v28p123/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v28p123/r4.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v28p123/r4.claim: Alternatively, if “He” refers to the preceding name of God, “Allah” is its predicate and al-Khaliq is an attribute.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v28p123/r4.anchor: فاسم الجلالة بعده خبر عنه و { الخالق } صفة

IBNASHUR-FULL:v28p123/r5.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v28p123/r5.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v28p123/r5.claim: Khaliq is an active participle of khalq, whose basic linguistic sense is bringing a thing into being in a particular form.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v28p123/r5.anchor: و { الخالق } : اسم فاعل من الخلق ، وأصل الخلق في اللغة إيجاد شيء

IBNASHUR-FULL:v28p123/r6.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v28p123/r6.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v28p123/r6.claim: Ibn ʿAshur had discussed the broader sense of creating forms in Jesus’ words about making a bird from clay, in 3:49.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v28p123/r6.anchor: وقد تقدم عند قوله تعالى حكاية عن عيسى عليه السلام { إني أخلق لكم من الطين

IBNASHUR-FULL:v28p123/r7.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v28p123/r7.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v28p123/r7.claim: Khalq can more narrowly mean bringing into existence what was absent; this is the dominant sense of God’s name al-Khaliq, with 50:38 as an example.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v28p123/r7.anchor: ويطلق الخلق على معنى أخص من إيجاد الصور وهو إيجاد ما لم يكن موجودا

IBNASHUR-FULL:v28p123/r8.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v28p123/r8.speaker: الكشاف
IBNASHUR-FULL:v28p123/r8.claim: Al-Kashshaf glosses al-Khaliq as the one who determines what He brings into being.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v28p123/r8.anchor: قال في ( الكشاف ) : ( المقدر لما يوجده )

IBNASHUR-FULL:v28p123/r9.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v28p123/r9.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v28p123/r9.claim: Ibn ʿAshur explains the Kashshaf gloss by God’s acts being measured by wisdom: khalq as bringing forth from nothing, broader than forming images; he cites 7:11 on one reading.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v28p123/r9.anchor: لما كانت إحداثات الله مقدرة بمقادير الحكمة عبر عن إحداثه بالخلق

IBNASHUR-FULL:v28p123/r10.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v28p123/r10.speaker: الراغب
IBNASHUR-FULL:v28p123/r10.claim: Al-Raghib defines khalq as sound proportioning, also used for originating something without prior material or a model to imitate.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v28p123/r10.anchor: وقال الراغب : الخلق التقدير المستقيم واستعمل في إيداع الشيء من غير أصل ولا احتذاء

IBNASHUR-FULL:v28p124/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v28p124/r1.speaker: ابن العربي
IBNASHUR-FULL:v28p124/r1.claim: Ibn al-ʿArabi defines al-Khaliq as bringing things from nonexistence to existence with their qualities, then ranks al-Bariʾ as narrower and al-Musawwir narrower still; Ibn ʿAshur says he blends two senses.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v28p124/r1.anchor: وقال أبو بكر ابن العربي في ( عارضة الأحوذي ) على ( سنن الترمذي ) :

IBNASHUR-FULL:v28p124/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v28p124/r2.speaker: الغزالي
IBNASHUR-FULL:v28p124/r2.claim: Al-Ghazali distinguishes three linked stages: measuring what will exist, bringing it into existence according to the measure, then arranging its forms beautifully; the names describe God by each stage.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v28p124/r2.anchor: وقال الغزالي في ( المقصد الأسنى ) : الخالق البارىء المصور قد يظن أن هذه الأسماء مترادفة

IBNASHUR-FULL:v28p124/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v28p124/r3.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v28p124/r3.claim: Al-Ghazali treats the three meanings as inseparable stages distinguished by perspective, but Ibn ʿAshur says this does not fit how these names are used.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v28p124/r3.anchor: فجعل المعاني متلازمة وجعل الفرق بينها بالاعتبار ، ولا أحسبه ينطبق

IBNASHUR-FULL:v28p124/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v28p124/r4.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v28p124/r4.claim: Al-Bariʾ is the active participle of the hamzated verb baraʾa.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v28p124/r4.anchor: و { البارىء } اسم فاعل من برأ مهموزا

IBNASHUR-FULL:v28p124/r5.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v28p124/r5.speaker: الكشاف
IBNASHUR-FULL:v28p124/r5.claim: Al-Kashshaf explains al-Bariʾ as differentiating what God brings into being from one another by their varied shapes; Ibn ʿAshur finds this distinct from al-Khaliq.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v28p124/r5.anchor: قال في ( الكشاف ) المميز لما يوجده بعضه من بعض بالأشكال المختلفة
