IBNASHUR-FULL:v28p124/r6.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v28p124/r6.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v28p124/r6.claim: The Qurʾanic phrase about the best and worst bariyya, plus the hadith and ʿAli’s saying, show that bariʾ is not restricted to human beings.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v28p124/r6.anchor: ومن كلام علي رضي الله عنه : لا والذي فلق الحبة وبرأ النسمة

IBNASHUR-FULL:v28p124/r8.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v28p124/r8.speaker: ابن العربي
IBNASHUR-FULL:v28p124/r8.claim: Ibn al-ʿArabi derives al-Bariʾ from dust and limits it to creating humankind, so al-bariyya in 98:6–7 means people.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v28p124/r8.anchor: وقال ابن العربي في ( العارضة ) : { البارىء } : خالق الناس من البرى

IBNASHUR-FULL:v28p124/r9.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v28p124/r9.speaker: ابن عطية
IBNASHUR-FULL:v28p124/r9.claim: Ibn ʿAtiyya explains al-Bariʾ as equivalent to al-Khaliq; the author says the lexicographer in al-Qamus does likewise.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v28p124/r9.anchor: وفسره ابن عطية بمعنى الخالق . وكذلك صاحب القاموس

IBNASHUR-FULL:v28p124/r10.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v28p124/r10.speaker: الغزالي
IBNASHUR-FULL:v28p124/r10.claim: Al-Ghazali glosses al-Bariʾ as the one who brings an existent into being, an interpretation Ibn ʿAshur says does not fit usage.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v28p124/r10.anchor: وفسره الغزالي بأنه الموجود المخترع ، وقد علمت أنه غير منطبق

IBNASHUR-FULL:v28p124/r11.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v28p124/r11.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v28p124/r11.claim: Among the proposed explanations of al-Bariʾ, Ibn ʿAshur judges the Kashshaf’s differentiation by forms to be best.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v28p124/r11.anchor: فأحسن تفسير له ما في ( الكشاف )

IBNASHUR-FULL:v28p124/r12.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v28p124/r12.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v28p124/r12.claim: Al-Musawwir is the one who forms the visible shapes of all creatures that have visible forms.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v28p124/r12.anchor: مكون الصور لجميع المخلوقات ذوات الصور المرئية

IBNASHUR-FULL:v28p125/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v28p125/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v28p125/r1.claim: Together the names portray divine origination in stages: bringing into existence, forming the human body, then granting its beautiful shape; Ibn ʿAshur links this to 82:7–8 and 3:6.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v28p125/r1.anchor: فابتدىء بالخلق الذي هو الإيجاد الأصلي ثم بالبرء الذي هو تكوين جسم الإنسان ثم بالتصور

IBNASHUR-FULL:v28p125/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v28p125/r2.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v28p125/r2.claim: After the earlier attributes, these names highlight God’s wondrous creation of people and awaken gratitude, which leads into the declaration that all creation glorifies Him.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v28p125/r2.anchor: ليثير داعية شكرهم على ذلك . ولذلك عقب بجملة { يسبح له ما في السماوات والأرض }

IBNASHUR-FULL:v28p125/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v28p125/r3.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v28p125/r3.claim: Ibn ʿAshur groups the closing attributes into three sets that correspond to the sūra’s subjects, while their order also follows local links such as analogy, precaution, or completion.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v28p125/r3.anchor: ينقسم إلى ثلاثة أقسام ولكنها ذكرت في الآية بحسب تناسب مواقع بعضها عقب بعض من تنظير أو احتراس أو تتميم

IBNASHUR-FULL:v28p126/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v28p126/r4.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v28p126/r4.claim: Al-Quddus, al-Muhaymin, al-Khaliq, al-Bariʾ, and al-Musawwir concern both groups in the sūra, each of whom receives their share of these attributes.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v28p126/r4.anchor: متعلق بما يشترك فيه الفريقان المذكوران في هذه السورة فيأخذ كل فريق حظه منها

IBNASHUR-FULL:v28p126/r5.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v28p126/r5.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v28p126/r5.claim: The closing phrase sums up God’s attributes, including those just listed; it calls them names because creation names Him by them and they reach perfect truth in relation to Him.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v28p126/r5.anchor: والمراد بالأسماء الصفات ، عبر عنها بالأسماء لأنه متصف بها على ألسنة خلقه

IBNASHUR-FULL:v28p126/r6.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v28p126/r6.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v28p126/r6.claim: The phrase points to the denotations of the names, as “He displayed them” in 2:31 means that God showed the named things to the angels.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v28p126/r6.anchor: والمقصود : أن له مدلولات الأسماء الحسنى كما في قوله تعالى : { ثم عرضهم على الملائكة

IBNASHUR-FULL:v28p126/r7.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v28p126/r7.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v28p126/r7.claim: Ibn ʿAshur notes the earlier command in 7:180 to call upon God by His beautiful names.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v28p126/r7.anchor: وقد تقدم قوله تعالى : { ولله الأسماء الحسنى فادعوه بها في سورة الأعراف . }

IBNASHUR-FULL:v28p126/r8.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v28p126/r8.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v28p126/r8.claim: The clause about glorification is circumstantial to “to Him belong the beautiful names.”
IBNASHUR-FULL:v28p126/r8.anchor: جملة { يسبح له } الخ في موضع الحال من ضمير { له الأسماء الحسنى }

IBNASHUR-FULL:v28p126/r9.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v28p126/r9.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v28p126/r9.claim: God’s beautiful attributes lead rational beings in the heavens and earth to exalt Him; knowledge of some names prompts every kind to glorify, intentionally or not.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v28p126/r9.anchor: يضطر ما في السماوات والأرض من العقلاء على تعظيمه بالتسبيح والتنزيه عن النقائص

IBNASHUR-FULL:v28p126/r10.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v28p126/r10.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v28p126/r10.claim: Even an atheist or naturalist who admires the universe’s order is in reality praising the free agent, although he calls it time or nature.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v28p126/r10.anchor: فالدهري أو الطبائعي إذا نوه بنظام الكائنات وأعجب بانتساقها فإنما يسبح في الواقع للفاعل المختار

IBNASHUR-FULL:v28p126/r11.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v28p126/r11.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v28p126/r11.claim: Glorification may mean spoken declaration of transcendence, or may include figurative glorification by the signs things present through their state.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v28p126/r11.anchor: فأما إن حمل على ما يشمل المعنيين الحقيقي والمجازي من دلالة على التنزيه ولو بلسان الحال

IBNASHUR-FULL:v28p126/r12.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v28p126/r12.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v28p126/r12.claim: On the broader figurative reading, created things’ provision and subjugation testify to God through the signs of their existence and order.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v28p126/r12.anchor: ما ثبت له من صفات الخلق والإمداد والقهر تدل عليه شواهد المخلوقات وانتظام وجودها

IBNASHUR-FULL:v28p127/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v28p127/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v28p127/r1.claim: “He is the Mighty, the Wise” is coordinated with the preceding circumstantial clause; these attributes aptly fit the order of creation.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v28p127/r1.anchor: عطف على جملة الحال وأوثر هاتان الصفتان لشدة مناسبتهما لنظام الخلق

IBNASHUR-FULL:v28p127/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v28p127/r2.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v28p127/r2.claim: The verse closes by returning to the sūra’s opening, forming a ring around the sūra.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v28p127/r2.anchor: وفي هذه الآية رد العجز على الصدر لأن صدر السورة مماثل لآخرها

IBNASHUR-FULL:v28p127/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v28p127/r3.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
IBNASHUR-FULL:v28p127/r3.claim: Al-Tirmidhi transmits with a hasan chain from Maʿqil ibn Yasar that reciting the refuge and the last three verses morning or evening brings 70,000 angels’ prayers until the opposite time; death that day or night is martyrdom.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v28p127/r3.anchor: روى الترمذي بسند حسن عن معقل بن يسار عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم قال : ( من قال حين يصبح ثلاث مرات

IBNASHUR-FULL:v28p127/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v28p127/r4.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
IBNASHUR-FULL:v28p127/r4.claim: A report passed from ʿAbd Allah ibn Masʿud through reciters and Gabriel says placing a hand on one’s head at 59:21 brings a cure for every illness except death; Ibn ʿAshur calls it a rare serial report to Gabriel.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v28p127/r4.anchor: فإني قرأت على النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم فلما بلغت هذه الآية قال لي : ضع يدك على رأسك فإن جبريل

IBNASHUR-FULL:v28p127/r5.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v28p127/r5.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
IBNASHUR-FULL:v28p127/r5.claim: Al-Daylami reports from ʿAli and Ibn Masʿud that reciting 59:21 through the end of the sūra is a spell for headache.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v28p127/r5.anchor: وأخرج الديلمي عن علي وابن مسعود عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم أنه قال في قوله تعالى : { لو أنزلنا هذا القرآن }

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p292/r2.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p292/r2.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p292/r2.claim: God then declares Himself above the unbelievers' association of idols with Him, since the idols possess none of these attributes.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p292/r2.anchor: ثم نزه الله تعالى نفسه عن إشراك الكفار به الأصنام التي ليس لها شيء من هذه الصفات،

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p292/r3.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p292/r3.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p292/r3.claim: Al-bāriʾ means creator: God brought creation into existence.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p292/r3.anchor: و: البارئ بمعنى الخالق، برأ الله الخلق أي أوجدهم،

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p292/r4.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p292/r4.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p292/r4.claim: Al-muṣawwir is the one who brings forms into existence.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p292/r4.anchor: و: المصور هو الذي يوجد الصور،

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p292/r5.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p292/r5.speaker: علي بن أبي طالب
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p292/r5.claim: ʿAlī read al-muṣawwira with accusative inflection, governed by al-bāriʾ; Ibn Atiyya calls it good and takes it generically of forms.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p292/r5.anchor: وقرأ علي بن أبي طالب: «المصور» بنصب الواو والراء على إعمال البارئ به، وهي حسنة

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p292/r6.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p292/r6.speaker: علي بن أبي طالب
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p292/r6.claim: Another reading attributed to ʿAlī has fatḥa on the wāw and kasra on the rāʾ, on the grammatical model of al-ḥasan al-wajh.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p292/r6.anchor: وقال قوم عن علي بن أبي طالب رضي الله عنه إنه قرأ: «المصور» بفتح الواو وكسر الراء

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p292/r7.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p292/r7.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p292/r7.claim: The beautiful names have beautiful meanings subsisting in God's essence; there is no deity but Him.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p292/r7.anchor: له الأسماء الحسنى أي ذات الحسن في معانيها القائمة بذاته لا إله إلا هو،

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p292/r8.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p292/r8.speaker: رسول الله
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p292/r8.claim: The Prophet says God has 99 names, one short of 100, and whoever counts them enters Paradise; al-Tirmidhī and others transmit the list.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p292/r8.anchor: إن الله تعالى تسعة وتسعين اسما، مائة إلا واحدا من أحصاها دخل الجنة

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p292/r9.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p292/r9.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p292/r9.claim: Although people disagree about some names, Ibn Atiyya says no specified list is soundly established; only the count and virtue of enumerating them are established without identifying them.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p292/r9.anchor: واختلف في بعضها ولم يصح فيها شيء إلا إحصاؤها دون تعين

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p228/r1.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p228/r1.speaker: الخطابي
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p228/r1.claim: Al-Khattabi defines al-Khaliq as the initiator and inventor of creatures without a prior model.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p228/r1.anchor: فقال الخطابي هو المتبدىء للخلق المخترع لهم على غير مثال سبق

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p228/r2.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p228/r2.speaker: زهير
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p228/r2.claim: In Zuhayr’s line, khalaqta means to plan something and then carry it out, unlike people who form wishes they never fulfill.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p228/r2.anchor: فأما في نعوت الآدميين فمعنى الخلق كقول زهير ولأنت تفري ما خلقت وبع

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p228/r3.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p228/r3.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p228/r3.claim: Al-Bari is the creator who brings creatures into being.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p228/r3.anchor: والبارئ الخالق يقال برأ الله الخلق يبرؤهم

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p228/r4.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p228/r4.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p228/r4.claim: Al-Musawwir gives creatures varied forms by delineating and shaping them so they can recognize one another.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p228/r4.anchor: والمصور الذي أنشأ خلته على صور مختلفة ليتعارفوا بها ومعنى التصوير التخطيط والتشكيل

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p228/r5.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p228/r5.speaker: الحسن وأبو الجوزاء وأبو عمران وابن السميفع
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p228/r5.claim: These readers pronounce the waw and raʾ of al-musawwar with fatḥa, making the word passive and referring it to Adam.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p228/r5.anchor: وقرأ الحسن وأبو الجوزاء وأبو عمران وابن السميفع البارئ المصور بفتح الواو والراء جميعا

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p228/r6.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p228/r6.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p228/r6.claim: Ibn al-Jawzi says the rest of the discussion was already explained at al-Aʿraf 7:180 and al-Israʾ 17:110 and onward.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p228/r6.anchor: وما بعد هذا قد تقدم بيانه الأعراف 180 والإسراء 110 إلى آخر السورة

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p80/r7.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p80/r7.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p80/r7.claim: Khalq is determining; baraʾ is cutting or carrying out, bringing the determined plan into existence, which only God can execute.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p80/r7.anchor: الخلق: التقدير، والبراء: هو الفري، وهو التنفيذ وإبراز ما قدره وقرره إلى الوجود، وليس كل من قدر شيئا

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p80/r8.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p80/r8.speaker: الشاعر
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p80/r8.claim: A poet praises someone who can execute what he has planned, unlike those who plan but cannot carry it out; Ibn Kathir uses the line to illustrate the distinction.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p80/r8.anchor: قال الشاعر يمدح آخر (5) ولأنت تفري ما خلقت … وبعض القوم يخلق ثم لا يفري

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p80/r9.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p80/r9.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p80/r9.claim: The idiom of a cutter measuring before cutting illustrates carrying out a design according to its intended measure.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p80/r9.anchor: ومنه يقال: قدر الجلاد ثم فرى، أي: قطع على ما قدره بحسب ما يريده.

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p80#2/r1.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p80#2/r1.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p80#2/r1.claim: When God wills a thing, He says Be and it is, with the quality and form He chooses; al-Musawwir brings it into existence in that chosen form.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p80#2/r1.anchor: وقوله تعالى: {الخالق البارئ المصور} أي: الذي إذا أراد شيئا قال له: كن، فيكون على الصفة التي يريد، والصورة التي يختار.

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p80#2/r2.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p80#2/r2.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p80#2/r2.claim: The phrase about God assembling a person in whatever form He wills (82:8) illustrates His power to fashion the chosen form.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p80#2/r2.anchor: كقوله: {في أي صورة ما شاء ركبك} [الانفطار: 8] ولهذا قال: {المصور} أي: الذي ينفذ ما يريد إيجاده على الصفة التي يريدها.

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p80#2/r3.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p80#2/r3.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p80#2/r3.claim: Ibn Kathir recalls the Ṣaḥīḥayn report from Abu Hurayra: God has ninety-nine names, and whoever enumerates them enters Paradise; God is One and loves odd numbers.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p80#2/r3.anchor: عن أبي هريرة، عن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم: "إن لله تعالى تسعة وتسعين اسما، مائة إلا واحدا، من أحصاها دخل الجنة

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p80#2/r4.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p80#2/r4.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p80#2/r4.claim: Al-Tirmidhi and Ibn Majah transmit an enumeration of the names with textual differences; Ibn Kathir says he has already detailed its routes and wordings.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p80#2/r4.anchor: وسياق ابن ماجه بزيادة ونقصان، وتقديم وتأخير، وقد قدمنا ذلك مبسوطا مطولا بطرقه وألفاظه

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p81/r1.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p81/r1.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p81/r1.claim: All in the heavens and earth glorifies God, as also stated in 17:44, though humans do not understand every creature's glorification.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p81/r1.anchor: كقوله {تسبح له السماوات السبع والأرض ومن فيهن وإن من شيء إلا يسبح بحمده ولكن لا تفقهون تسبيحهم إنه كان حليما غفورا} [الإسراء: 44] .

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p81/r2.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p81/r2.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p81/r2.claim: Al-ʿAzīz is inviolable and unassailable; al-Ḥakīm is wise in God's law and decree.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p81/r2.anchor: أي: فلا يرام جنابه {الحكيم} في شرعه وقدره.

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p81/r3.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p81/r3.speaker: معقل بن يسار
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p81/r3.claim: The Prophet promises that whoever seeks refuge from Satan in the morning or evening and recites the last three verses of al-Hashr will have 70,000 angels pray for him; if he dies that day, he dies a martyr. Al-Tirmidhi calls the report gharīb, known only by this chain.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p81/r3.anchor: عن معقل بن يسار، عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم قال: "من قال حين يصبح ثلاث مرات: أعوذ بالله السميع العليم من الشيطان الرجيم

KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p509/r10.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p509/r10.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p509/r10.claim: Al-khāliq is the one who determines what He brings into existence.

KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p509/r11.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p509/r11.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p509/r11.claim: Al-bāriʾ distinguishes created things from one another through their different forms.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p509/r11.anchor: المميز بعضه من بعض بالأشكال المختلفة

KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p509/r12.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p509/r12.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p509/r12.claim: Al-muṣawwir is the one who gives form.

KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p509/r13.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p509/r13.speaker: حاطب بن أبي بلتعة
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p509/r13.claim: Ḥāṭib reads al-bāriʾ al-muṣawwir with fatḥa on the wāw and accusative rāʾ, meaning the one who creates the form-giver and differentiates what it forms by varied shapes.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p509/r13.anchor: وعن حاطب بن أبي بلتعة أنه قرأ : ( البارىء المصور ) ، بفتح الواو ونصب الراء

KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p509/r14.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p509/r14.speaker: ابن مسعود
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p509/r14.claim: Ibn Masʿūd reads “and whatever is in the earth,” omitting the reference to the heavens.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p509/r14.anchor: وقرأ ابن مسعود : ( وما في الأرض )

KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p509/r15.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p509/r15.speaker: أبو هريرة
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p509/r15.claim: Abū Hurayra reports asking the Prophet about God's greatest name; the Prophet tells him to read the end of al-Hashr often, repeating the answer when asked again.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p509/r15.anchor: عن أبي هريرة رضي الله عنه

KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p509/r16.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p509/r16.speaker: رسول الله
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p509/r16.claim: The Prophet says whoever recites Sūrat al-Hashr will have earlier and later sins forgiven; no grading is stated.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p509/r16.anchor: عن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم

BURSEVI:v9p376#2/r1.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v9p376#2/r1.speaker: التأويلات النجمية
BURSEVI:v9p376#2/r1.claim: Al-Tawīlāt al-Najmiyya reads the names as indicating God's oneness in essence and attributes, wise governance, transcendence from contingent defects, bringing things from nonexistence into being, preserving them, honoring friends, subduing enemies, manifesting majesty in all forms, and transcending all association.
BURSEVI:v9p376#2/r1.anchor: وفي التأويلات النجمية قوله سبحانه هو الله الذي لا إله إلا هو الملك الخ يشير إلى وحدانية ذاته وفردانية صفاته

BURSEVI:v9p376#2/r2.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v9p376#2/r2.speaker: البقلي
BURSEVI:v9p376#2/r2.claim: Al-Baqli's ʿArāʾis reads associating partners with God through the eyes and thoughts as what the declaration of divine transcendence excludes.
BURSEVI:v9p376#2/r2.anchor: وفي عرائس البقلي سبحان الله عما يشركون إليه بالنواظر والخواطر

BURSEVI:v9p376#2/r3.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v9p376#2/r3.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v9p376#2/r3.claim: Al-Khāliq means the measurer of things according to wisdom and will; the root's original sense is measurement, as in shaping a shoe to a measure, whether creation uses material or not.
BURSEVI:v9p376#2/r3.anchor: أصل معنى الخلق التقدير كما يقال خلق النعل إذا قدرها وسواها بمقياس

BURSEVI:v9p376#2/r4.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v9p376#2/r4.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v9p376#2/r4.claim: The servant of al-Khāliq measures things according to God's intent because the divine attribute of creating and measuring is disclosed to him; he plans only by God's determination.
BURSEVI:v9p376#2/r4.anchor: وعبد الخالق هو الذي يقدر الأشياء على وفق مراد الحق لتجليه له بوصف الخلق والتقدير

BURSEVI:v9p376#2/r5.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v9p376#2/r5.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v9p376#2/r5.claim: Reciting al-Khāliq for an hour or more in the middle of the night is said to illuminate the reciter's heart and face.
BURSEVI:v9p376#2/r5.anchor: وخاصية هذا الاسم أن يذكر في جوف الليل ساعة فما فوقها فيتنور قلب ذاكره ووجهه

BURSEVI:v9p376#2/r6.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v9p376#2/r6.speaker: السهروردي
BURSEVI:v9p376#2/r6.claim: The Idrīsī invocation calls God creator of all in the heavens and earth; al-Suhrawardī prescribes 5,000 recitations for recovering lost things or reaching an absent person far away.
BURSEVI:v9p376#2/r6.anchor: وفي الأربعين الإدريسية خالق من في السموات ومن في الأرض وكل إليه معاده قال السهروردي يذكر لجمع الضائع

BURSEVI:v9p376#2/r7.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v9p376#2/r7.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v9p376#2/r7.claim: Al-Bāriʾ originates things without disparity or deficiency, in accord with wise measure and complete benefit.
BURSEVI:v9p376#2/r7.anchor: الموجد للأشياء بريئة من التفاوت فإن البرء الإيجاد على وجه يكون الموجد بريئا من التفاوت والنقصان

BURSEVI:v9p376#2/r8.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v9p376#2/r8.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v9p376#2/r8.claim: The servant of al-Bāriʾ makes work balanced and consistent, doing what fits the divine name; the source connects this to the absence of disparity in God's creation.
BURSEVI:v9p376#2/r8.anchor: وعبد البارىء هو الذي يبرأ عمله من التفاوت والاختلاف فلا يفعل إلا ما يناسب حضرة الاسم البارىء

BURSEVI:v9p376#2/r9.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v9p376#2/r9.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v9p376#2/r9.claim: Reciting al-Bāriʾ one hundred times daily for seven consecutive days is prescribed for protection from afflictions, even in the grave.
BURSEVI:v9p376#2/r9.anchor: وخاصية هذا الاسم أن يذكره سبعة أيام متوالية كل يوم مائة مرة للسلامة من الآفات

BURSEVI:v9p376#2/r10.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v9p376#2/r10.speaker: السهروردي
BURSEVI:v9p376#2/r10.claim: Al-Suhrawardī says the Idrīsī invocation to al-Bāriʾ opens wealth, honor, and safety from afflictions; writing the invocation on pitch and hanging it on a mad person or someone with a severe illness is said to help.
BURSEVI:v9p376#2/r10.anchor: قال السهروردي يفتح لذاكره أبواب الغنى والعز والسلامة من الآفات وإذا كتب في لوح من قير وعلق على المجنون نفعه

BURSEVI:v9p376#2/r11.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v9p376#2/r11.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v9p376#2/r11.claim: Al-Muṣawwir brings the forms and qualities of things into existence as He wills; He gives every created thing its form.
BURSEVI:v9p376#2/r11.anchor: الموجد لصور الأشياء وكيفياتها كما أراد

BURSEVI:v9p378#2/r1.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v9p378#2/r1.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v9p378#2/r1.claim: The names are most beautiful because they indicate beautiful meanings, as discussed earlier in Sūrat Ṭā Hā.
BURSEVI:v9p378#2/r1.anchor: لدلالتها على المعاني الحسنة كما سبق في سورة طه

BURSEVI:v9p378#2/r2.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v9p378#2/r2.speaker: الكاشفي
BURSEVI:v9p378#2/r2.claim: Al-Kāshifī says God's names are beautiful by the standards of both revelation and reason.
BURSEVI:v9p378#2/r2.anchor: قال الكاشفي : مر اوراست نامهاى نيكى

BURSEVI:v9p378#2/r3.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v9p378#2/r3.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v9p378#2/r3.claim: Al-ḥusnā is the feminine superlative of al-aḥsan, just as al-ʿulyā is feminine for al-aʿlā.
BURSEVI:v9p378#2/r3.anchor: والحسنى صيغة تفضيل لأنها تأنيث الأحسن كالعليا في تأنيث الأعلى

BURSEVI:v9p378#2/r4.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v9p378#2/r4.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v9p378#2/r4.claim: Calling the names absolutely most beautiful signifies unsurpassed excellence: God's names and essence have no comparison with the names or essences of others.
BURSEVI:v9p378#2/r4.anchor: وتوصيف الأسماء بها للزيادة المطلقة إذ لا نسبة لأسمائه إلى غير الأسماء من أسماء الغير

BURSEVI:v9p378#2/r5.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v9p378#2/r5.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v9p378#2/r5.claim: A hadith gives God's names as ninety-nine.
BURSEVI:v9p378#2/r5.anchor: وأسماء الله تسعة وتسعون على ما جاء في الحديث

BURSEVI:v9p378#2/r6.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v9p378#2/r6.speaker: الرازي
BURSEVI:v9p378#2/r6.claim: Al-Rāzī says he saw a dhikr book listing four thousand names: a thousand each in the Qurʾān and sound reports, Torah, Gospel, and Psalms.
BURSEVI:v9p378#2/r6.anchor: ونقل صاحب اللباب عن الإمام الرازي أنه قال : رأيت في بعض كتب الذكر

BURSEVI:v9p378#2/r7.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v9p378#2/r7.speaker: النبي عليه السلام
BURSEVI:v9p378#2/r7.claim: The Prophet's supplication invokes every name God used for Himself, revealed in a book, taught to a creature, or reserved in knowledge of the unseen; the author suggests ninety-nine names are the best-known and most comprehensive.
BURSEVI:v9p378#2/r7.anchor: روي إن من دعاء رسول الله عليه السلام : أسألك بكل اسم سميت به نفسك

BURSEVI:v9p378#2/r8.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v9p378#2/r8.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v9p378#2/r8.claim: The multiplicity of names does not entail multiple named beings: one person may be called father, grandfather, uncle, or scholar from different relations while remaining one.
BURSEVI:v9p378#2/r8.anchor: وتعدد الأسماء لا يدل على تعدد المسمى لأن الواحد يسمى أبا من وجه وجدا من وجه وخالا

BURSEVI:v9p378#2/r9.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v9p378#2/r9.speaker: عبد الرحمن البسطامي
BURSEVI:v9p378#2/r9.claim: Al-Bisṭāmī describes a retreat practice of taking the abjad value of a divine name, omitting the definite article, and reciting that exact number in a quiet place under the conditions of retreat to obtain a timely response.
BURSEVI:v9p378#2/r9.anchor: قال عبد الرحمن البسطامي قدس سره في ترويح القلوب : اعلم أن من السر المكتوم في الدعاء

BURSEVI:v9p378#2/r10.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v9p378#2/r10.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v9p378#2/r10.claim: The author explains that exceeding the prescribed number is waste and falling short is a defect; a name's count is like a key's teeth, opening the door of answered prayer.
BURSEVI:v9p378#2/r10.anchor: فإن الزيادة على العدد المطلوب إسراف والنقص منه إخلال والعدد في الذكر بالأسماء كأسنان المفتاح

BURSEVI:v9p378#2/r11.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v9p378#2/r11.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v9p378#2/r11.claim: Knowers attend to the article and the word's root in divine names, while the Malāmiyya omit the article as an addition beyond the root.
BURSEVI:v9p378#2/r11.anchor: ثم اعلم أن العارفين يلاحظون في الأسماء آلة التعريف وأصل الكلمة والملامية يطرحون منها آلة التعريف

BURSEVI:v9p378#2/r12.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v9p378#2/r12.speaker: العلماء
BURSEVI:v9p378#2/r12.claim: Scholars define a name as a conventional expression for a meaning, the named as that meaning, and naming as assigning or applying the expression.
BURSEVI:v9p378#2/r12.anchor: قال العلماء : الاسم هو اللفظ الدال على المعنى بالوضع

BURSEVI:v9p378#2/r13.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v9p378#2/r13.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v9p378#2/r13.claim: Some scholars hold that naming God is restricted to terms found in the Qurʾān or an authentic hadith.
BURSEVI:v9p378#2/r13.anchor: وإطلاق الاسم على الله تعالى توقفي عند البعض

BURSEVI:v9p378#2/r14.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v9p378#2/r14.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v9p378#2/r14.claim: Other scholars allow any term whose meaning befits God's majesty.
BURSEVI:v9p378#2/r14.anchor: وقال آخرون : كل لفظ دل على معنى

BURSEVI:v9p378#3/r1.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v9p378#3/r1.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v9p378#3/r1.claim: The restrictive view cites God's established descriptions as ʿĀlim, ʿAlīm, and ʿAllām, while rejecting unattested terms such as ʿĀrif, Faqīh, and Mutayaqqin.
BURSEVI:v9p378#3/r1.anchor: ومن أدلة الأولين أن الله عالم بلا مرية فيقال له عالم وعليم وعلام

BURSEVI:v9p378#3/r2.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v9p378#3/r2.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v9p378#3/r2.claim: The permissive view argues that Muslim consensus accepts fitting descriptions in Persian, Turkish, and Indian, even though those words are absent from scripture.
BURSEVI:v9p378#3/r2.anchor: ومن أدلة الآخرين أن الأسماءوصفاته مذكورة بالفارسية والتركية والهندية

BURSEVI:v9p378#3/r3.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v9p378#3/r3.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v9p378#3/r3.claim: The permissive view invokes 17:110: God commands people to call on Him by the most beautiful names, which are beautiful because they denote perfect attributes; meaning, not the wording alone, is decisive.
BURSEVI:v9p378#3/r3.anchor: ومنها أن الله تعالى قال : ولله الأسماء الحسنى فادعوه بها والاسم لا يحسن إلا لدلالته على صفات الكمال

BURSEVI:v9p378#3/r4.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v9p378#3/r4.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v9p378#3/r4.claim: A newly coined term that suggests an unsuitable meaning is discourteous, but a term conveying a sound, beautiful meaning without a repugnant implication is not disrespectful.
BURSEVI:v9p378#3/r4.anchor: غاية ما في الباب أن يكون وضع الاسم علما له مستحدثا

MAWARDI-FULL:v5p513/r25.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p513/r25.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p513/r25.claim: Al-Khaliq is the one who brings things into existence according to His will.

MAWARDI-FULL:v5p513/r26.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p513/r26.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p513/r26.claim: Alternatively, al-Khaliq is the one who determines things with wisdom.

MAWARDI-FULL:v5p513/r27.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p513/r27.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p513/r27.claim: Al-Bari may mean the one who distinguishes creatures, as in the expression meaning I separated myself from him.
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p513/r27.anchor: المميز للخلق , ومنه قوله : برئت منه

MAWARDI-FULL:v5p513/r28.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p513/r28.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p513/r28.claim: It may also mean the one who originates creation; a cited line supports that sense.

MAWARDI-FULL:v5p514/r1.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p514/r1.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p514/r1.claim: The cited poetry supports al-Bari as the one who brings creation into being.
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p514/r1.anchor: براك الله حين براه غيثا ويجري منك أنهارا عذابا

MAWARDI-FULL:v5p514/r2.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p514/r2.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p514/r2.claim: Al-Musawwir may mean shaping each creature according to God's will when it is first created.

MAWARDI-FULL:v5p514/r3.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p514/r3.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p514/r3.claim: Alternatively, it means giving each kind its own form and producing each generation in that established form; both readings demonstrate God's power.
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p514/r3.anchor: وعلى الوجه الثاني يكون محمولا على ما استقر من صور الخلق

MAWARDI-FULL:v5p514/r4.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p514/r4.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p514/r4.claim: A third possibility is moving humans and animals through successive forms, from sperm to clot to flesh and finally old age, as al-Nabigha's line illustrates.
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p514/r4.anchor: ثم مضغة إلى أن يصير شيخا هرما , كما قال النابغة

MAWARDI-FULL:v5p514/r5.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p514/r5.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p514/r5.claim: All God's names are beautiful because they derive from His beautiful attributes.
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p514/r5.anchor: أن جميع أسمائه حسنى لاشتقاقه من صفاته الحسنى

MAWARDI-FULL:v5p514/r6.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p514/r6.speaker: الكلبي
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p514/r6.claim: Al-Kalbi says the phrase means God has the highest exemplars or qualities.
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p514/r6.anchor: أن له الأمثال العليا , قاله الكلبي

MUQATIL:59:24/r1.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:59:24/r1.speaker: author
MUQATIL:59:24/r1.claim: God creates everything, including the drop of seed and the clinging lump.
MUQATIL:59:24/r1.anchor: يعنى خالق كل شىء خلق النطفة والمضغة

MUQATIL:59:24/r2.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:59:24/r2.speaker: author
MUQATIL:59:24/r2.claim: Al-Bari means that God forms souls from the lump of flesh into a human, giving eyes, ears, hands, and feet.
MUQATIL:59:24/r2.anchor: فجعل له العينين، والأذنين، واليدين، والرجلين

MUQATIL:59:24/r3.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:59:24/r3.speaker: author
MUQATIL:59:24/r3.claim: God shapes people in wombs as he wills: male or female, white or black, sound or unsound.
MUQATIL:59:24/r3.anchor: { المصور } في الأرحام، كيف يشاء ذكر وأثنى، أبيض وأسود، سوي وغير سوي

MUQATIL:59:24/r4.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:59:24/r4.speaker: author
MUQATIL:59:24/r4.claim: The beautiful names include al-Rahman, al-Rahim, al-Aziz, al-Jabbar, and al-Mutakabbir, among the names cited in the surah.
MUQATIL:59:24/r4.anchor: يعني الرحمن الرحيم العزيز الجبار المتكبر، ونحوها من الأسماء يعني هذه الأسماء التي ذكرها في هذه السورة

MUQATIL:59:24/r5.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:59:24/r5.speaker: author
MUQATIL:59:24/r5.claim: Everything in the heavens and earth remembers God and declares his oneness.
MUQATIL:59:24/r5.anchor: يعنى يذكره ويوحده ما في السموات والأرض وما فيها من الخلق وغيره

MUQATIL:59:24/r6.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:59:24/r6.speaker: author
MUQATIL:59:24/r6.claim: God is mighty in his dominion and wise in his command.
MUQATIL:59:24/r6.anchor: { وهو العزيز } في ملكه { الحكيم } [آية: 24] في أمره

MUQATIL:59:24/r7.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:59:24/r7.speaker: author
MUQATIL:59:24/r7.claim: Al-Rahim is gentler than al-Rahman, describing one who turns compassionately toward creation with mercy.
MUQATIL:59:24/r7.anchor: الرحيم أرق من الرحمن يعني المترحم يعني المتعطف بالرحمة على خلقه

MUQATIL:59:24/r8.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:59:24/r8.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
MUQATIL:59:24/r8.claim: A report attributed to the Prophet says God has ninety-nine names in the Quran and whoever enumerates them enters Paradise; another strand transmits it through Abu Hurayra.
MUQATIL:59:24/r8.anchor: قال: " إن لله تسعة وتسعين اسما في القرآن فمن أحصاها دخل الجنة "

MUQATIL:59:24/r9.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:59:24/r9.speaker: المسيب
MUQATIL:59:24/r9.claim: Al-Musayyib glosses saying Subhan Allah as declaring God free of evil.
MUQATIL:59:24/r9.anchor: عن المسيب، قال سبحان الله: انصاف الله من السوء

MUQATIL:59:24/r10.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:59:24/r10.speaker: علي بن أبي طالب
MUQATIL:59:24/r10.claim: Ali ibn Abi Talib says Subhan Allah is a phrase that God approved for himself.
MUQATIL:59:24/r10.anchor: وقال علىي بن أبي طالب، رضي الله عنه: سبحان الله كلمة رضيها الله لنفسه

MUQATIL:59:24/r11.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:59:24/r11.speaker: مقاتل
MUQATIL:59:24/r11.claim: Muqatil says Quranic tasbih generally declares God free of evil, but in the opening of al-Isra and in Ya-Sin it expresses wonder; in al-Rum it means pray.
MUQATIL:59:24/r11.anchor: وقال الهذيل: قال مقاتل: سبحان الله في القرآن تنزيه نزه نفسه، من السوء إلا أول بني إسرائيل

MUQATIL:59:24/r12.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:59:24/r12.speaker: مطرف بن الشخير
MUQATIL:59:24/r12.claim: Mutarrif ibn al-Shikhkhir says God did not leave people to predestination in the Quran.
MUQATIL:59:24/r12.anchor: عن مطرف بن الشخير، قال: إن الله تعالى لم يكلنا في القرآن على القدر

NASAFI-FULL:v4p235#2/r1.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v4p235#2/r1.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v4p235#2/r1.claim: Al-Khāliq is the One who determines what He brings into existence.

NASAFI-FULL:v4p235#2/r2.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v4p235#2/r2.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v4p235#2/r2.claim: Al-Bāriʾ is the One who brings things into existence.
NASAFI-FULL:v4p235#2/r2.anchor: الموجد ﴿ المصور ﴾ في الارحام ﴿ له الأسماء الحسنى ﴾

NASAFI-FULL:v4p235#2/r3.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v4p235#2/r3.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v4p235#2/r3.claim: Al-Muṣawwir shapes creatures in the wombs.
NASAFI-FULL:v4p235#2/r3.anchor: في الارحام ﴿ له الأسماء الحسنى ﴾ الدالة على الصفات العلا

NASAFI-FULL:v4p235#2/r4.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v4p235#2/r4.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v4p235#2/r4.claim: The beautiful names indicate God's sublime attributes.

NASAFI-FULL:v4p235#2/r5.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v4p235#2/r5.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v4p235#2/r5.claim: The sūra closes with the theme with which it began.

NASAFI-FULL:v4p235#2/r6.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v4p235#2/r6.speaker: أبو هريرة
NASAFI-FULL:v4p235#2/r6.claim: Abū Hurayra says he asked the Messenger about God's greatest name; the Prophet directed him to the end of al-Ḥashr and told him to recite it often.
NASAFI-FULL:v4p235#2/r6.anchor: عن أبي هريرة رضي الله عنه سألت حبيبي رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم عن الاسم الاعظم فقال عليك بآخر الحشر فأكثر قراءته

QURTUBI-FULL:59:24/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:59:24/r1.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:59:24/r1.claim: Al-Khaliq here means the one who determines or measures out creation.
QURTUBI-FULL:59:24/r1.anchor: { الخالق } هنا المقدر. و { البارىء } المنشىء المخترع

QURTUBI-FULL:59:24/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:59:24/r2.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:59:24/r2.claim: Al-Bariʾ means the initiator who brings things into existence.
QURTUBI-FULL:59:24/r2.anchor: و { البارىء } المنشىء المخترع. و { المصور } مصور الصور

QURTUBI-FULL:59:24/r3.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:59:24/r3.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:59:24/r3.claim: Al-Musawwir forms images and arranges them in differing configurations; forming is the final stage, following creation and origination.
QURTUBI-FULL:59:24/r3.anchor: و { المصور } مصور الصور ومركبها على هيئات مختلفة

QURTUBI-FULL:59:24/r4.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:59:24/r4.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:59:24/r4.claim: God forms the human in the womb through three stages: a clot, then a lump, then a recognizable shape and distinguishing appearance.
QURTUBI-FULL:59:24/r4.anchor: جعله علقة، ثم مضغة، ثم جعله صورة وهو التشكيل

QURTUBI-FULL:59:24/r5.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:59:24/r5.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:59:24/r5.claim: Some equate creation with image-making, but Qurtubi rejects this order: determining is first, origination next, and shaping last.
QURTUBI-FULL:59:24/r5.anchor: وقد جعل بعض الناس الخلق بمعنى التصوير، وليس كذلك

QURTUBI-FULL:59:24/r6.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:59:24/r6.speaker: النابغة
QURTUBI-FULL:59:24/r6.claim: Al-Nabigha's verse names the creator, originator, and shaper in sequence and describes the stages in the womb.
QURTUBI-FULL:59:24/r6.anchor:
وقال النابغة:
الخالق البارىء المصور في ال

QURTUBI-FULL:59:24/r7.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:59:24/r7.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:59:24/r7.claim: Qurtubi cites Zuhayr to distinguish executing a plan from merely conceiving it: other people can plan what they cannot successfully carry out.
QURTUBI-FULL:59:24/r7.anchor: يقول: تقدر ما تقدر ثم تفريه، أي تمضيه على وفق تقديرك

QURTUBI-FULL:59:24/r8.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:59:24/r8.speaker: حاطب بن أبي بلتعة
QURTUBI-FULL:59:24/r8.claim: Hatib ibn Abi Baltaʿa read al-bariʾ al-musawwira with the waw vowelled in fatḥa and the ra accusative, meaning the one who brings forth or distinguishes the portrayed forms by their varying configurations; al-Zamakhshari reports it.
QURTUBI-FULL:59:24/r8.anchor: وعن حاطب ابن أبي بلتعة أنه قرأ «البارىء المصور» بفتح الواو ونصب الراء

QURTUBI-FULL:59:24/r9.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:59:24/r9.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:59:24/r9.claim: The verse attributes the most beautiful names to God and says everything in heaven and earth glorifies Him; Qurtubi refers readers to his earlier discussion.
QURTUBI-FULL:59:24/r9.anchor: له الأسماء الحسنى يسبح له ما في السماوات والأرض وهو العزيز الحكيم

QURTUBI-FULL:59:24/r10.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:59:24/r10.speaker: أبو هريرة
QURTUBI-FULL:59:24/r10.claim: Abu Hurayra asked the Prophet about God's greatest name and was told to recite the end of Surat al-Hashr often; no grading is stated.
QURTUBI-FULL:59:24/r10.anchor: وعن أبي هريرة قال: سألت خليل أبا القاسم رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم عن اسم الله الأعظم

QURTUBI-FULL:59:24/r11.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:59:24/r11.speaker: جابر بن زيد
QURTUBI-FULL:59:24/r11.claim: Jabir ibn Zayd identifies Allah itself as the greatest name, pointing to this verse.
QURTUBI-FULL:59:24/r11.anchor: وقال جابر بن زيد: إن اسم الله الأعظم هو الله لمكان هذه الآية

QURTUBI-FULL:59:24/r12.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:59:24/r12.speaker: أنس بن مالك
QURTUBI-FULL:59:24/r12.claim: Anas reports the Prophet promising forgiveness of past and future sins to whoever recites Surat al-Hashr; no grading is stated.
QURTUBI-FULL:59:24/r12.anchor: وعن أنس بن مالك: أن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم قال

QURTUBI-FULL:59:24#2/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:59:24#2/r1.speaker: أبو أمامة
QURTUBI-FULL:59:24#2/r1.claim: Abu Umama reports the Prophet saying that whoever recites the concluding verses of al-Hashr by day or night and dies that day or night is guaranteed Paradise; no grading is stated.
QURTUBI-FULL:59:24#2/r1.anchor: من قرأ خواتم سورة الحشر في ليل أو نهار فقبضه الله في تلك الليلة

RAZI-FULL:v29p256#2/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v29p256#2/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v29p256#2/r1.claim: Al-Khāliq means determining or measuring acts according to specific forms, so the attribute of creating relates to God's will.
RAZI-FULL:v29p256#2/r1.anchor: والخلق هو التقدير معناه أنه يقدر أفعاله على وجوه مخصوصة ،

RAZI-FULL:v29p256#2/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v29p256#2/r2.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v29p256#2/r2.claim: Al-Bāriʾ means maker or bringer into existence, specifically the origination of bodies; creatures are called bariyyah, but accidents such as color and taste are not.
RAZI-FULL:v29p256#2/r2.anchor: وهو بمنزلة قولنا : صانع وموجد إلا أنه يفيد اختراع الأجسام

RAZI-FULL:v29p256#2/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v29p256#2/r3.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v29p256#2/r3.claim: Al-Muṣawwir is the One who creates the forms of creatures as He wills.
RAZI-FULL:v29p256#2/r3.anchor: فمعناه أنه يخلق صور الخلق على ما يريد

RAZI-FULL:v29p256#2/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v29p256#2/r4.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v29p256#2/r4.claim: The order reflects causal priority: choosing the measure by will precedes power's effect, and creating essences precedes creating their attributes.

RAZI-FULL:v29p256#2/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v29p256#2/r5.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v29p256#2/r5.claim: He refers readers to his earlier explanation of God's beautiful names.
RAZI-FULL:v29p256#2/r5.anchor: وقد فسرناه في قوله : { ولله الأسماء الحسنى }

RAZI-FULL:v29p256#2/r6.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v29p256#2/r6.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v29p256#2/r6.claim: He refers readers to his earlier explanation of all that is in the heavens and earth glorifying God.
RAZI-FULL:v29p256#2/r6.anchor: فقد مر تفسيره في أول سورة الحديد

TAB-FULL:v22p555#2/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v22p555#2/r1.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v22p555#2/r1.claim: God alone is worthy of worship and is the sole Creator; no other being deserves worship or creates alongside Him.
TAB-FULL:v22p555#2/r1.anchor: المصور خلقه كيف شاء، وكيف يشاء

TAB-FULL:v22p555#2/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v22p555#2/r2.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v22p555#2/r2.claim: Al-Bariʾ is the One who brings creation into existence by His power.
TAB-FULL:v22p555#2/r2.anchor: المصور خلقه كيف شاء، وكيف يشاء

TAB-FULL:v22p555#2/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v22p555#2/r3.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v22p555#2/r3.claim: Al-Musawwir shapes His creation however He wills.
TAB-FULL:v22p555#2/r3.anchor: المصور خلقه كيف شاء، وكيف يشاء

TAB-FULL:v22p556/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v22p556/r1.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v22p556/r1.claim: The most beautiful names belong to God: these are the names by which He named Himself and mentioned in the preceding two verses.
TAB-FULL:v22p556/r1.anchor: في تدبيره خلقه، وصرفهم فيما فيه صلاحهم

TAB-FULL:v22p556/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v22p556/r2.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v22p556/r2.claim: Everything in the heavens and earth glorifies and prostrates to God, willingly or unwillingly.
TAB-FULL:v22p556/r2.anchor: في تدبيره خلقه، وصرفهم فيما فيه صلاحهم

TAB-FULL:v22p556/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v22p556/r3.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v22p556/r3.claim: Al-Aziz means that God is severe in vengeance against His enemies.
TAB-FULL:v22p556/r3.anchor: في تدبيره خلقه، وصرفهم فيما فيه صلاحهم

TAB-FULL:v22p556/r4.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v22p556/r4.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v22p556/r4.claim: Al-Hakim describes God's wise governance and direction of creation toward what benefits them.
TAB-FULL:v22p556/r4.anchor: في تدبيره خلقه، وصرفهم فيما فيه صلاحهم

TABATABAI:59:24/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:59:24/r1.speaker: author
TABATABAI:59:24/r1.claim: The Creator brings things into being by determination, the Originator distinguishes them from each other, and the Fashioner gives them distinct forms; the progression is creation, origination, then forming.
TABATABAI:59:24/r1.anchor: الخالق هو الموجد للأشياء عن تقدير

TABATABAI:59:24/r2.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:59:24/r2.speaker: author
TABATABAI:59:24/r2.claim: The previous two verses introduce their eleven names with God’s exclusive divinity because lordship and sovereign management entail rightful worship; this verse introduces names of creation instead.
TABATABAI:59:24/r2.anchor: لأن الأسماء الكريمة المذكورة في الآيتين السابقتين وهي أحد عشر اسما من لوازم الربوبية

TABATABAI:59:24/r3.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:59:24/r3.speaker: author
TABATABAI:59:24/r3.claim: God’s exclusive creation does not by itself establish exclusive divinity: idolaters acknowledge Him as Creator while still worshipping other lords and claiming partners.
TABATABAI:59:24/r3.anchor: لا يستوجب اختصاص الألوهية به كما يدل عليه أن الوثنيين قائلون

TABATABAI:59:24/r4.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:59:24/r4.speaker: author
TABATABAI:59:24/r4.claim: Allah is the proper name of the Essence that gathers all perfections, to which the other names apply; repeating it at the start of all three verses strengthens the point.
TABATABAI:59:24/r4.anchor: فهو علم للذات المستجمع لجميع صفات الكمال يرتبط به ويجري عليه جميع الأسماء وفي التكرار مزيد تأكيد

TABATABAI:59:24/r5.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:59:24/r5.speaker: author
TABATABAI:59:24/r5.claim: The definite plural with the article indicates the entirety of the remaining beautiful names.
TABATABAI:59:24/r5.anchor: إشارة إلى بقية الأسماء الحسنى عن آخرها لكون الأسماء جمعا محلى باللام وهو يفيد العموم

TABATABAI:59:24/r6.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:59:24/r6.speaker: author
TABATABAI:59:24/r6.claim: Everything in the universe glorifies God, including the heavens and earth themselves.
TABATABAI:59:24/r6.anchor: أي جميع ما في العالم من المخلوقات حتى نفس السماوات والأرض

TABATABAI:59:24/r7.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:59:24/r7.speaker: author
TABATABAI:59:24/r7.claim: Al-ʿAzīz means the unconquered victor; al-Ḥakīm means that His acts are precise and never arbitrary.
TABATABAI:59:24/r7.anchor: الغالب غير المغلوب الذي فعله متقن لا مجازفة فيه

TABATABAI:59:24/r8.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:59:24/r8.speaker: author
TABATABAI:59:24/r8.claim: Ending with these names signals that the Qur’an comes from the Mighty and Wise, who cannot be defied and does not waste obedience or the reward of the good; this explains repeating Mighty alongside Wise.
TABATABAI:59:24/r8.anchor: والعناية إلى ختم الكلام بالاسمين والإشارة بذلك إلى كون القرآن النازل من عنده كلام عزيز حكيم

TABRISI:59:23-24/r3.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:59:23-24/r3.speaker: author
TABRISI:59:23-24/r3.claim: Al-Khaliq means the creator of bodies and their accidents.
TABRISI:59:23-24/r3.anchor: للأجسام والأعراض المخصوصة. وقيل: المقدر للأشياء

TABRISI:59:23-24/r4.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:59:23-24/r4.speaker: قيل
TABRISI:59:23-24/r4.claim: Another explanation calls God the determiner of things by wisdom who brings them into existence by His will.
TABRISI:59:23-24/r4.anchor: وقيل: المقدر للأشياء بحكمته المحدث للأشياء على إرادته

TABRISI:59:23-24/r5.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:59:23-24/r5.speaker: author
TABRISI:59:23-24/r5.claim: Al-Bariʾ is the one who originates creation and makes bodies and accidents.

TABRISI:59:23-24/r6.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:59:23-24/r6.speaker: author
TABRISI:59:23-24/r6.claim: Al-Musawwir shapes bodies in their diverse forms, such as animals and inanimate things.
TABRISI:59:23-24/r6.anchor: الذي صور الأجسام على اختلافها مثل الحيوان والجماد

TABRISI:59:23-24/r7.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:59:23-24/r7.speaker: author
TABRISI:59:23-24/r7.claim: The beautiful names include Allah, the Merciful, the Compassionate, the Powerful, the Knowing, and the Living; the commentary discussed this in al-Aʿraf.
TABRISI:59:23-24/r7.anchor: نحو الله الرحمن الرحيم القادر العالم الحي وقد مر بيانه في سورة الأعراف

TABRISI:59:23-24/r8.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:59:23-24/r8.speaker: author
TABRISI:59:23-24/r8.claim: All things glorify God: living beings verbally declare His transcendence, while inanimate things indicate it.
TABRISI:59:23-24/r8.anchor: أي ينزهه جميع الأشياء فالحي يصفه بالتنزيه والجماد يدل على تنزيهه

TABRISI:59:23-24/r9.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:59:23-24/r9.speaker: رسول الله
TABRISI:59:23-24/r9.claim: The Prophet says God's greatest name occurs in six verses at the end of Surat al-Hashr.
TABRISI:59:23-24/r9.anchor: قال رسول صلى الله عليه وسلم

THALABI:v9p288/r5.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v9p288/r5.speaker: author
THALABI:v9p288/r5.claim: Al-Khaliq is the determiner who, through governing, transforms a thing from one state to another; the author links this to creation in successive stages and to humans being made in stages.
THALABI:v9p288/r5.anchor: الخالق المقدر المقلب للشيء بالتدبير الى غيره كما قال: يخلقكم في بطون أمهاتكم خلقا من بعد خلق وقال: خلقكم أطوارا

THALABI:v9p288/r6.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v9p288/r6.speaker: author
THALABI:v9p288/r6.claim: Al-Bariʾ is the one who brings individual entities from nonexistence into existence.
THALABI:v9p288/r6.anchor: البارئ المنشئ للأعيان من العدم الى الوجود المصور الممثل للمخلوقات

THALABI:v9p288/r7.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v9p288/r7.speaker: author
THALABI:v9p288/r7.claim: Al-Musawwir gives creatures their forms, distinguishing signs, and varied appearances so that some can be distinguished from others; ṣūra means a thing's likeness.
THALABI:v9p288/r7.anchor: المصور الممثل للمخلوقات والعلامات المميزة والهيئات المتفرقة حتى يتميز بها بعضها من بعض يقال: هذه صورة الأمر

THALABI:v9p288/r8.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v9p288/r8.speaker: author
THALABI:v9p288/r8.claim: The author distinguishes stages of formation: creation first, then the embryo as a drop and clot, then shaping when it is completed.
THALABI:v9p288/r8.anchor: فأولا يكون خلقا ثم [نطفة ثم علقة] ثم تصويرا إذا انتهى وكمل

THALABI:v9p288/r9.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v9p288/r9.speaker: عبد الله بن عمر
THALABI:v9p288/r9.claim: Ibn Umar reports that the Prophet, recounting God's words, said that on Judgment Day God will gather the seven heavens and earth in His grasp and declare a series of divine names; the excerpt breaks off mid-list.
THALABI:v9p288/r9.anchor: قال عبد الله بن عمر: رأيت رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم قائما على هذا المنبر

BURHAN:v1p341/r3.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v1p341/r3.speaker: author
BURHAN:v1p341/r3.claim: The anomalous passive participle المُصوَّر is construed as the object of البارئ, which works like a verb: ‘the one who created the formed one.’
BURHAN:v1p341/r3.anchor: بفتح الواو والراء على أنه اسم مفعول وتأويله أنه مفعول لاسم الفاعل

BURHAN:v3p473/r6.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v3p473/r6.speaker: author
BURHAN:v3p473/r6.claim: Tadʿīd is a sequence of uncoordinated words, especially descriptors: their shared subject and referent make them function like adjectives. Divine attributes are therefore often listed without conjunction.
BURHAN:v3p473/r6.anchor: التعديد هي إيقاع الألفاظ المبددة على سياق واحد وأكثر ما يؤخذ في الصفات ومقتضاها ألا يعطف بعضها على بعض

ITQAN:v3p186/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v3p186/r1.speaker: author
ITQAN:v3p186/r1.claim: The successive divine attributes “Creator, Originator, Fashioner” function as praise and glorification.
ITQAN:v3p186/r1.anchor: الثالث المدح والثناء ومنه صفات الله تعالى

SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r5#5/r6.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r5#5/r6.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r5#5/r6.claim: Ḥadīd does not follow tasbīḥ with talk of earth's people, whereas the opening of Ḥashr moves to the People of the Book; Ḥashr 24 also uses a single ما without such a follow-up.
SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r5#5/r6.anchor: فأنت ترى أنه في آيات الحديد لم يعقب التسبيح بالكلام على أهل الأرض

NASHR:v1p250/r1.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v1p250/r1.speaker: النبي
NASHR:v1p250/r1.claim: A report attributed to the Prophet says that reciting the formula three times in the morning, then the last three verses of al-Hashr, brings 70,000 angels' prayers until evening and martyrdom if one dies that day; evening recitation has the same merit. al-Tirmidhi grades it hasan gharīb.
NASHR:v1p250/r1.anchor: من قال حين يصبح ثلاث مرات أعوذ بالله السميع العليم من الشيطان الرجيم
